punctuated: 諸侯也。」論《大學》之條目有曰：「身修而后家齊，家齊而后國治，國治而后天下平。」此則推行先後之序也。然約而言之，亦不越乎一敬而已。夫敬者，一心之主宰，萬事之本根，千聖相傳之心法，帝學成始成終之要道。堯之允恭，舜之恭己，禹之祗承，湯之懋敬，文王之懿恭，武王之執競，此敬也；《易》之乾乾，《書》之精一，《詩》之思無邪，《春秋》之謹嚴，《禮》之毋不敬，此敬也。皇上誠能存此心之敬而蘊之為德，以此德而達之于治，紀綱文章以此敬德而著，政教號令本此敬德而推，殆見治隆俗美，內平外成，三辰迭運而不失其宜，四時順行而不拂其序，山川鬼神莫不以寧，鳥獸魚鱉罔不咸若，可以為堯舜，可以參天地、賛化育，而保天下之事備矣，継志述事之道盡矣。《周書》有之曰：「王敬作所，不可不敬德。」程子曰：「涵養須用敬。」此之謂也。臣學不足以致君澤民，謹竭愚陋以獻，惟皇上采擇焉，則不勝幸甚。臣謹對。
translation_en:
… the feudal lords.” And in discussing the steps of the Great Learning (Daxue), it is said: “Only after the person is cultivated is the family regulated; only after the family is regulated is the state rightly governed; only after the state is rightly governed is the world at peace.” This, then, is the proper sequence of priority in putting governance into practice. Yet, to sum it up briefly, this too does not go beyond the single word “reverence” (jing).

For reverence is the master of the single mind, the root of the myriad affairs, the method of the mind transmitted across a thousand sages, and the essential Way by which imperial learning achieves both its beginning and its end. Yao’s sincere courtesy, Shun’s reverent self-composure, Yu’s respectful compliance, Tang’s strenuous reverence, King Wen’s admirable courtesy, and King Wu’s steadfast vigor—all of these are this reverence. The unceasing diligence of the Book of Changes (Yi), the subtle refinement and single-mindedness of the Book of Documents (Shu), the “having no depraved thoughts” of the Book of Odes (Shi), the strictness and gravity of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and the “never failing in reverence” of the Book of Rites (Li)—all of these are this reverence.

If Your Majesty can truly preserve this reverence of the mind and store it up within as virtue, and through this virtue extend it to governance—so that fundamental laws and institutional patterns are made manifest through this reverent virtue, and governance, instruction, decrees, and commands are extended on the basis of this reverent virtue—then we shall surely see governance flourish and customs grow virtuous, the interior pacified and the exterior brought to order, the three luminaries revolving in alternation without losing their proper measure, the four seasons proceeding smoothly without violating their sequence, mountains, rivers, ghosts, and spirits all enjoying tranquility, and birds, beasts, fishes, and turtles all following their natures. Thus Your Majesty can become like Yao and Shun, can form a triad with Heaven and Earth and assist in their transforming and nourishing work; the task of preserving the Empire will be complete, and the Way of carrying on the intentions and continuing the enterprises of Your ancestors will be fulfilled to the utmost.

The Documents of Zhou (Zhoushu) has it: “May the King make reverence his resting place; he cannot but hold virtue in reverence.” Master Cheng (Chengzi) said: “Self-cultivation requires the use of reverence.” This is what is meant.

Your servant’s learning is insufficient to bring perfection to his Sovereign or bestow blessings upon the people; I respectfully exhaust my foolish and crude thoughts to offer them up. If only Your Majesty will deign to select from them, I shall be fortunate beyond measure. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
臣楊鼎
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心
盖心者妙是道之體用實致治之本原也苟存
其心則道由是而出治可得而善矣不存其心
則道由是而昧雖欲善治其可得乎稽諸往古
堯之欽明文思舜之溫恭允塞此二帝之所以
神明其心以妙夫道也禹之惟精惟一湯之以
禮制心文王之小心翼翼武王之無貳爾心此
三王之所以持其心以求夫道也故曰二帝三
王存此心者也欽惟
===
皇帝陛下禀聰明睿智之資備剛健中正之德纘承
列聖之洪圖尊居九五之大位遠宗帝王之道近守
祖宗之法道已至矣望之猶若未至民已安矣視之
猶若未安乃於萬幾之暇又進臣等於
廷賜以
清問首舉帝王為治之道繼以謹始圖成之要推
行之序此皆
陛下之所素知而素行者也豈待愚臣之言哉雖然
臣有以知
陛下之心即古昔聖人不自滿足之心好問好察之

猶若未安乃於萬幾之暇又進臣等於
廷賜以
清問首舉帝王爲治之道繼以謹始圖成之要推
行之序此皆
陛下之所素知而素行者也豈待愚臣之言哉雖然
臣有以知
陛下之心即古昔聖人不自滿足之心好問好察之
punctuated:
臣楊鼎。

臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。盖心者，妙是道之體用，實致治之本原也。苟存其心，則道由是而出，治可得而善矣；不存其心，則道由是而昧，雖欲善治，其可得乎？稽諸往古，堯之欽明文思，舜之溫恭允塞，此二帝之所以神明其心以妙夫道也；禹之惟精惟一，湯之以禮制心，文王之小心翼翼，武王之無貳爾心，此三王之所以持其心以求夫道也。故曰：二帝、三王，存此心者也。欽惟皇帝陛下，禀聰明睿智之資，備剛健中正之德，纘承列聖之洪圖，尊居九五之大位，遠宗帝王之道，近守祖宗之法。道已至矣，望之猶若未至；民已安矣，視之猶若未安。乃於萬幾之暇，又進臣等於廷，賜以清問，首舉帝王為治之道，繼以謹始圖成之要、推行之序。此皆陛下之所素知而素行者也，豈待愚臣之言哉？雖然，臣有以知陛下之心，即古昔聖人不自滿足之心、好問好察之
translation_en:
Your servant Yang Ding 楊鼎.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings was rooted in the Way, and that the Way of the Emperors and Kings was rooted in the mind. For the mind subtles the substance and function of this Way, and is truly the fundamental source for bringing about good governance. If one preserves one's mind, then the Way issues forth from it, and governance can thereby be perfected; if one does not preserve one's mind, then the Way is obscured by this, and even though one might wish for good governance, how could it be attained? Examining remote antiquity: Yao's 堯 reverence, intelligence, Accomplishment, and thoughtfulness, and Shun's 舜 mildness, respectfulness, and sincere integrity—these were whereby the Two Emperors made their minds spiritually luminous so as to subtle the Way. Yu's 禹 refinement and single-mindedness, Tang's 湯 regulating the mind through ritual, King Wen's 文王 cautious and reverent care, and King Wu's 武王 "have no duplicity in your hearts"—these were whereby the Three Kings upheld their minds so as to seek the Way. Therefore it is said: the Two Emperors and Three Kings were those who preserved this mind.

Reverently I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty is endowed with intelligent, perspicacious, and wise qualities, and possesses firm, vigorous, balanced, and upright virtue. Succeeding to the grand enterprise of the line of Former Sages and occupying in majesty the great throne of the Nine-in-the-Fifth, You take as Your distant model the Way of the Emperors and Kings, and closely observe the laws of Your Imperial Ancestors. The Way has already reached its utmost, yet You look toward it as though it had not yet been reached; the people are already at peace, yet You regard them as though they were not yet at peace. Thus, in the leisure from myriad affairs of state, You have further brought Your servants before the Court and favored us with Your sagely inquiry, first raising the Way of governance of the Emperors and Kings, and following with the essentials of being careful at the beginning to plan for completion, as well as the sequence for putting them into practice. All of these are what Your Majesty has long known and long practiced—how could they await the words of a foolish servant? Even so, Your servant has the means to know that Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind of the sages of antiquity, who were never self-satisfied and who loved to question and examine…

意也臣雖淺陋欽承
清問敢不拜手稽首以對揚
聖天子之明命乎臣切惟經者聖人載道之器二帝
三王為治之道具載於其間孔子以天縱之聖
任斯道之重當周轍既東之日而不得君師之
位於是退於洙泗之間刪詩書定禮樂讚周易
脩春秋纂集而成六經以為萬世楷範後世人
主有志於二帝三王之道皆可舉而行之若夫
漢承秦而有天下享國四百年中間賢智之君
若武帝之雄才大畧舉用賢能罷黜百家表章
===
六經光武之講論經理勤勞不怠首訪儒雅興
起學校當時若董仲舒之儒術鄧禹之勳業皆
有可稱焉唐繼隋而有天下享國三百年中間
賢智之君若太宗之力行仁義身致太平憲宗
憤積世之弊憫唐室之替善用忠謀不惑群議
當時若房玄齡杜如晦之善謀善斷若李絳之
清直皆有可取焉至於宋有天下若太祖太宗
真宗之為君皆嚮慕隆古時則有若趙普之沉
毅呂蒙正李沆之剛正亦皆足以有為焉君臣
之相遇如此而其致治成功宜可追乎二帝三

毅呂蒙正李沆之剛正亦皆足以有爲焉君臣
之相遇如此而其致治成功宜可追乎二帝三
punctuated: 意也。臣雖淺陋，欽承清問，敢不拜手稽首以對揚聖天子之明命乎！臣切惟經者，聖人載道之器，二帝三王為治之道具載於其間。孔子以天縱之聖，任斯道之重，當周轍既東之日，而不得君師之位，於是退於洙泗之間，刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，讚《周易》，脩《春秋》，纂集而成六經，以為萬世楷範。後世人主有志於二帝三王之道，皆可舉而行之。若夫漢承秦而有天下，享國四百年，中間賢智之君，若武帝之雄才大畧，舉用賢能，罷黜百家，表章六經；光武之講論經理，勤勞不怠，首訪儒雅，興起學校；當時若董仲舒之儒術，鄧禹之勳業，皆有可稱焉。唐繼隋而有天下，享國三百年，中間賢智之君，若太宗之力行仁義，身致太平；憲宗憤積世之弊，憫唐室之替，善用忠謀，不惑群議；當時若房玄齡、杜如晦之善謀善斷，若李絳之清直，皆有可取焉。至於宋有天下，若太祖、太宗、真宗之為君，皆嚮慕隆古；時則有若趙普之沉毅，呂蒙正、李沆之剛正，亦皆足以有為焉。君臣之相遇如此，而其致治成功，宜可追乎二帝三
translation_en:
… intent [to love asking and examining]. Although your servant is shallow and crude, having reverently received Your Majesty's gracious inquiry, how dare I not bow with hands clasped and touch my head to the ground to respond to and extol the bright mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven! Your servant humbly reflects that the Classics are the vessels by which the sages conveyed the Way, and the Way of governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings is recorded in full within them. Confucius, with his Heaven-endowed sageliness, took upon himself the heavy burden of this Way. Living in the days after the Zhou royal house had moved east, and unable to attain the position of ruler and teacher, he retired to the region between the Zhu and Si rivers. There he pruned the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), fixed the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), wrote commentaries on the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi), and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), collecting and editing them to form the Six Classics as a model and standard for ten thousand generations. Any ruler of later ages who aspired to the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings could take them up and put them into practice.

As for the Han, which succeeded the Qin in possessing All under Heaven and enjoyed the state for four hundred years, among its worthy and wise rulers were Emperor Wu (Wudi), who possessed heroic talent and grand strategy, promoted and employed the worthy and capable, dismissed the hundred schools, and exalted the Six Classics; and Emperor Guangwu, who discussed and expounded the principles of the Classics, was diligent and untiring, first sought out refined Confucian scholars, and revived schools. At those times, the Confucian learning of Dong Zhongshu and the meritorious achievements of Deng Yu were both worthy of praise. The Tang succeeded the Sui in possessing All under Heaven and enjoyed the state for three hundred years. Among its worthy and wise rulers were Emperor Taizong, who vigorously practiced benevolence and righteousness and personally brought about great peace; and Emperor Xianzong, who resented the accumulated abuses of generations, lamented the decline of the Tang house, excelled at adopting loyal counsel, and was not led astray by the opinions of the crowd. At those times, the skill in planning and decisiveness of Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, as well as the purity and uprightness of Li Jiang, all had much to recommend them. Coming to the Song's possession of All under Heaven, rulers such as Emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Zhenzong all admired and yearned for high antiquity. In those times there were men like Zhao Pu with his deep resolve, and Lü Mengzheng and Li Hang with their firm uprightness, all of whom were likewise capable of great accomplishment. With rulers and ministers meeting in such a way, their realization of good governance and achievement of success ought to have been able to rival those of the Two Emperors and Three…

punctuated: 王也。然漢不免於雜伯，唐不免於雜夷，宋亦不過大綱正而萬目未盡舉。比之《詩》、《書》所稱，所謂「於變時雍」、「比屋可封」、《關睢》《麟趾》之風、《鵲巢》《騶虞》之化，有所不及者，盖由其君徒欲其治而不求其道，徒有其志而不求其心；為之臣者，或於道有未聞，或用之未盡其才。此漢、唐、宋之治效所以止於漢、唐、宋而已也。洪惟天朝，太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝丕隆大統於前，仁宗昭皇帝、宣宗章皇帝紹承令緒於後，咸以帝王之心而求帝王之道，以帝王之道而為帝王之治，所以舉斯世於雍煕泰和之域，措斯民於春臺玉燭之中。至治之盛，巍巍然而無加，蕩蕩乎其難名，誠有如陛下所言矣。陛下以聖繼聖，嗣大歷服，允懷繼述，夙夜匪遑，期與臣民咸躋煕皞。
translation_en:
… Kings. Yet the Han did not escape admixing the ways of the hegemon, the Tang did not escape admixing barbarian customs, and the Song merely kept the great outlines rectified while failing to attend fully to the myriad details. Compared with what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu)—such as "Oh, they were transformed into concordant harmony," "house after house was worthy of enfeoffment," the customs of "Guanju" and "Linzhi," and the moral transformation of "Quechao" and "Zouyu"—they fell short. This was because their rulers merely desired good governance without seeking its Way, and merely possessed the ambition without seeking its mind; as for those who served as their ministers, some had not yet heard the Way, while others were employed without having their talents fully exhausted. This is why the efficacy of governance in the Han, Tang, and Song stopped merely at being that of the Han, Tang, and Song.

Reflecting grandly upon our Celestial Dynasty, Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu Gao Huangdi), and Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong Wen Huangdi), grandly exalted the Great Succession before, while Emperor Zhao, the Benevolent Ancestor (Renzong Zhao Huangdi), and Emperor Zhang, the Propagating Ancestor (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi), continued and inherited the fine patrimony after. All of them used the mind of the Emperors and Kings to seek the Way of the Emperors and Kings, and used the Way of the Emperors and Kings to enact the governance of the Emperors and Kings. Thus they raised this world into a realm of harmonious brightness and supreme peace, and placed this people amidst the Spring Terrace and the Jade Candle of seasonable harmony. The flourishing of utmost governance is so lofty that nothing can be added to it, and so vast that it is difficult to name—truly just as Your Majesty has stated.

Your Majesty, succeeding sages as a sage, has inherited the great succession and royal robes, sincerely cherishing the continuation and transmission of your predecessors' work, taking no leisure from morning to night, and hoping to ascend together with your ministers and people to a state of bright and serene harmony.

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
陛下之心即帝王兢兢業業求惟至道之心即
列聖敦崇古道以隆至治之心也
陛下以是心謹始而圖成推是心行之而得宜足以
為帝王之治又必拳拳以此策臣者夫豈徒哉
亦欲臣等而為帝王之臣也以臣之淺陋
陛下尚以帝王之臣望之
陛下以聖人之德而居聖人之位臣安敢不以帝王
之道陳之精一執中建中建極此帝王相傳授
之心法也
陛下常存之於一心始終而不易則謹始圖成之要
豈不在茲歟脩身齊家治國平天下此帝王推
行之序也
陛下運之於一心循其序而行之則脩己安人之宜
夫豈不得乎此固
清問之所及臣既俯伏而復其萬一矣臣於篇終
竊有獻焉臣切覩
陛下於龍飛之初開
經筵之講絕玩遊之娛減省之條常頒寬恤之詔
屢下此真存心帝王之道於其始也臣伏願
陛下始終此心始終此道始終此治建立大本經綸

punctuated: 陛下之心，即帝王兢兢業業、求惟至道之心，即列聖敦崇古道、以隆至治之心也。陛下以是心謹始而圖成，推是心行之而得宜，足以為帝王之治。又必拳拳以此策臣者，夫豈徒哉？亦欲臣等而為帝王之臣也。以臣之淺陋，陛下尚以帝王之臣望之；陛下以聖人之德而居聖人之位，臣安敢不以帝王之道陳之？精一執中，建中建極，此帝王相傳授之心法也。陛下常存之於一心，始終而不易，則謹始圖成之要，豈不在茲歟？脩身、齊家、治國、平天下，此帝王推行之序也。陛下運之於一心，循其序而行之，則脩己安人之宜，夫豈不得乎？此固清問之所及，臣既俯伏而復其萬一矣。臣於篇終，竊有獻焉。臣切覩陛下於龍飛之初，開經筵之講，絕玩遊之娛，減省之條常頒，寬恤之詔屢下，此真存心帝王之道於其始也。臣伏願陛下始終此心，始終此道，始終此治，建立大本，經綸
translation_en:
Your Majesty's mind is indeed the mind of the emperors and kings of old, who were cautious and diligent in seeking the supreme Way, and it is the mind of the successive sacred ancestors, who earnestly revered the ancient Way in order to exalt consummate governance. With this mind, Your Majesty is careful about the beginning and plans for completion; extending this mind to put it into practice appropriately is sufficient to achieve the governance of the emperors and kings of old. That You furthermore earnestly pose this policy question to Your servant—how could it be in vain? It is also because You wish for Your servants to become ministers worthy of the emperors and kings of old. Shallow and ignorant as Your servant is, Your Majesty still expects me to be a minister of the emperors and kings of old; since Your Majesty possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of a sage, how dare Your servant not set forth the Way of the emperors and kings of old?

"Being discerning and undivided, holding fast to the Mean," and "establishing the Mean and establishing the standard of perfection"—this is the method of the mind transmitted from one emperor and king to another. If Your Majesty constantly preserves this in Your single mind, never changing from beginning to end, then does not the essential way of being careful about the beginning and planning for completion lie right here? Cultivating the person, regulating the family, rightly governing the state, and making the whole realm peaceful and happy—this is the sequence of implementation followed by the emperors and kings. If Your Majesty operates this within Your single mind, following its sequence to put it into practice, then how could the appropriate measure for cultivating Yourself and bringing peace to others not be attained?

These are indeed the matters touched upon in Your august inquiry, and Your servant has prostrated himself and replied to one ten-thousandth of them. Yet at the end of this essay, Your servant ventures to offer a further word. Your servant has humbly observed that at the very beginning of Your Majesty's ascension to the throne, You inaugurated the Classics Colloquium lectures, abstained from the pleasures of sightseeing and recreation, regularly promulgated articles on retrenchment and reduction of expenditures, and repeatedly issued edicts of leniency and relief. This is truly keeping Your mind fixed on the Way of the emperors and kings at the beginning. Your servant humbly prays that Your Majesty will maintain this mind from beginning to end, maintain this Way from beginning to end, and maintain this governance from beginning to end, establishing the great foundation and ordering the …

translation_en: … the great invariable relations, so that Heaven and Earth will find their proper places and the myriad things will be nourished, every household will have a Hou Ji or a Xie, and customs will become like those of Zou and Lu. This can truly rival the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings in beauty; why then could the perfection of the end not be achieved? If so, it will not only be the utmost good fortune for your servants, but indeed the utmost good fortune for all under Heaven! Your servant is ignorant and benighted, unworthy to present a grand reply; I only pray that Your Majesty may deign to cast Your wise gaze upon it. Your servant is overcome with trembling and awe. Your servant respectfully replies.

punctuated:
臣倪謙。

臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，帝王之道具於經。經所以載道，而心者又所以具是道之全體，妙是道之大用也。故《易》以道陰陽，即人心太極之理也；《書》以道政事，即人心體用之跡也；《詩》以理性情，即人心勸懲之道也；《春秋》正名分，即人心褒貶之公也；《禮》以節事，《樂》以道志，即人心中和之理也。唐、虞、三代之君，所以繼天而立人極者，由其道具於心，治本於道，而底雍熈泰和之盛。漢、唐以来之君，所以莫能臻者，由其心與道二，治與道違，無怪其治之不古若也。洪惟太祖高皇帝膺天明命，撫有萬國，聖謨大訓，戒飭臣工，與古先哲王之道實相脗合。逮夫太宗文皇帝肅清內難，奠安宗社，萬幾之暇，表章六經，治道之盛，光前裕後。仁宗昭皇帝綂紹鴻業，宣宗章皇帝丕纘舊章，列聖相承，敦崇古道，以隆至治。巍乎成功，煥乎文章，
translation_en:
Your servant Ni Qian 倪謙.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way (dao 道), and that the Way of emperors and kings is embodied in the Classics (jing 經). The Classics are the vehicle that conveys the Way, while the mind is that which encompasses the complete substance of this Way and wondrously manifests its great function. Therefore, the Book of Changes (Yi 易) speaks of yin and yang, which is none other than the principle of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極) in the human mind; the Book of Documents (Shu 書) speaks of affairs of government, which is none other than the trace of substance and function in the human mind; the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) regulates human nature and emotions, which is none other than the Way of encouragement and warning in the human mind; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) rectifies names and statuses, which is none other than the impartiality of praise and blame in the human mind; the Book of Rites (Li 禮) moderates affairs and the Book of Music (Yue 樂) guides the will, which is none other than the principle of equilibrium and harmony in the human mind. The reason the rulers of Tang 唐 [Yao], Yu 虞 [Shun], and the Three Dynasties (Sandai 三代) were able to succeed Heaven and establish the ultimate standard for humankind was that the Way was embodied in their minds and their governance was rooted in the Way, thereby reaching the flourishing heights of harmonious peace and great concord. The reason the rulers from the Han 漢 and Tang 唐 dynasties onward have been unable to attain this is that their minds and the Way were divided into two, and their governance ran counter to the Way; it is no wonder that their governance did not match that of antiquity.

Humbly reflecting upon how Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝) received Heaven's illustrious mandate and pacified and possessed the myriad states: his sacred counsels and great instructions admonishing the officials truly tallied with the Way of the ancient sage-kings. Coming down to Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong Wen Huangdi 太宗文皇帝), he swept away internal difficulties and brought stability to the ancestral altars; in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he honored and promoted the Six Classics (Liujing 六經), and the flourishing of his Way of governance glorified his predecessors and enriched his successors. Benevolent Ancestor, Emperor Zhao (Renzong Zhao Huangdi 仁宗昭皇帝) carried on the great enterprise in full succession, and Proclaiming Ancestor, Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi 宣宗章皇帝) grandly continued the established statutes. Successive sacred emperors have inherited one another's work, earnestly esteeming the ancient Way so as to exalt supreme governance. How lofty their achievements, how brilliant their cultural institutions…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
猗歟盛哉伏惟
皇帝陛下嗣大歷服懋圖化理秉奉
天子民之誠隆繼志述事之孝道已躋於皇極世已
底於熈皡而猶不自滿暇日引儒臣講論墳典
切劘治道廼復進臣等于
廷降賜
清問且以允懐繼述夙夜匪遑為言其與帝舜之
惟時惟幾成湯之日新又新文王日昃不暇成
王緝熈單心同一揆也臣雖愚昧敢不拜手稽
首以對揚
===
===
聖天子之明命臣聞六經未作而帝王之道具乎太
極六經既作而帝王之道載諸方䇿為治者固
不可離經以求道又豈能離道以出治哉孔子
生於周末有德無位懼三綱淪而九法斁也廼
退而刪詩書定禮樂賛周易脩春秋纂而成之
肇自唐虞訖于周以為萬世楷範書之精一執
中建中建極二帝三王之心法可舉而行也詩之
關雎麟趾王道之端周南之風化可舉而行也
易之分爻立象莫非治體之要春秋褒善貶惡
無非經國之典然六經之道同歸而禮樂之用

極六經既作而帝王之道載諸方策爲治者固
不可離經以求道又豈能離道以出治哉孔子
生於周末有德無位懼三綱淪而九法斁也迺

易之爻象莫非治體之要春秋褒善貶惡
無非經國之典然六經之道同歸而禮樂之用
punctuated:
猗歟盛哉！伏惟皇帝陛下嗣大歷服，懋圖化理，秉奉天子民之誠，隆繼志述事之孝。道已躋於皇極，世已底於熈皡，而猶不自滿，暇日引儒臣講論墳典，切劘治道。廼復進臣等于廷，降賜清問，且以允懐繼述、夙夜匪遑為言。其與帝舜之惟時惟幾，成湯之日新又新，文王日昃不暇，成王緝熈單心，同一揆也。臣雖愚昧，敢不拜手稽首以對揚聖天子之明命？

臣聞《六經》未作，而帝王之道具乎太極；《六經》既作，而帝王之道載諸方䇿。為治者固不可離經以求道，又豈能離道以出治哉？孔子生於周末，有德無位，懼三綱淪而九法斁也，廼退而刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，賛《周易》，脩《春秋》，纂而成之，肇自唐、虞，訖于周，以為萬世楷範。《書》之精一執中、建中建極，二帝三王之心法可舉而行也；《詩》之《關雎》、《麟趾》，王道之端，《周南》之風化可舉而行也；《易》之分爻立象，莫非治體之要；《春秋》褒善貶惡，無非經國之典。然《六經》之道同歸，而《禮》、《樂》之用
translation_en:
… Oh, how magnificent! I humbly reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, having succeeded to the great dynastic mandate, earnestly plans for transformative governance, holding fast to the sincerity of serving Heaven and treating the people as your children, and exalting the filial piety of carrying forward the intentions and continuing the enterprises of your predecessors. The Way has already ascended to the August Ultimate, and the world has already reached a state of prosperous peace; yet You are still not self-satisfied, and in moments of leisure You summon Confucian scholars to expound upon and discuss the ancient canons, earnestly deliberating on the principles of governance. Now You have again summoned Your servants to the Court, condescending to bestow Your pure inquiries, and moreover speaking of sincerely cherishing the continuation of ancestral achievements and taking no leisure from morning to night. This is on the very same plane as Emperor Shun's being attentive to the moment and to the subtle beginnings, Cheng Tang's daily renewal and ever-continuing renewal, King Wen's allowing himself no leisure even past midday, and King Cheng's continuing the radiant legacy with all his heart. Though Your servant is ignorant and benighted, how dare I not bow my head to the ground upon my hands to respond to and extol the bright mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven?

Your servant has heard that before the Six Classics were composed, the Way of the Emperors and Kings was complete in the Supreme Ultimate; once the Six Classics were composed, the Way of the Emperors and Kings was recorded on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. Those who govern assuredly cannot depart from the Classics to seek the Way, and how could they depart from the Way to produce good governance? Confucius was born at the end of the Zhou dynasty; possessing virtue but lacking official position, and fearing that the Three Bonds would sink into oblivion and the Nine Categories of the Grand Norm would be ruined, he withdrew to edit the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of Documents (Shu), establish the Record of Rites (Li) and the Classic of Music (Yue), write commentaries on the Zhou Changes (Zhouyi), and compile the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). Collecting and completing them, beginning from Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and ending with the Zhou, he made them a model for ten thousand generations. In the Documents, "being discerning and undivided, holding fast the Mean," and "establishing the Mean and establishing the Ultimate"—this method of the mind of the Two Emperors and Three Kings can be taken up and put into practice. In the Poetry, the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes—the beginnings of the Kingly Way and the moral transformation of the "Zhounan" section—can be taken up and put into practice. In the Changes, the division of lines and establishment of hexagram images are nothing less than the essentials of the substance of governance; the Spring and Autumn Annals, in praising the good and censuring the evil, is nothing less than a canon for ordering the state. Yet while the Way of the Six Classics leads to the same end, the application of the Rites and Music…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
為急此孔子所以繼承往聖開萬世之太平也
爰暨漢唐以來賢智之君莫不景仰徽猷遹遵
彝典用圖治寧咸有稱述姑舉一二以實之若
漢武帝之罷黜百家表章六經光武之投戈講
藝息馬論道唐太宗之周禮一書乙夜勤讀固
為美矣其視堯舜禹湯文武授受之心法果何
如哉當時賢人君子出膺世用者亦莫不獻忠
效謀以匡乃辟若董仲舒以經術顯汲黯以忠
鯁著鄧禹立功名於光武魏徵勸仁義於太宗
固可尚矣其視臯夔伊傅周召都俞密勿之事
===
業果何如哉是以考論漢唐君臣之治功比之
詩書所稱則有所不及者以其雜伯雜夷徒有
願治之名而無躬行之實以為致理之本也恭
惟
陛下體二帝三王之心尊六經孔子之道監
祖宗之成憲以隆太平之治心與道相涵道與治相
安禮樂教化無非精神心術之著見典章文物
莫匪虛靈知覺之運行是以四海乂安萬邦協
和而躋斯世於熈皞者是皆
陛下夙夜匪遑躬行之所致也而又策臣以謹始圖

punctuated:
為急。此孔子所以繼承往聖、開萬世之太平也。
爰暨漢、唐以來，賢智之君莫不景仰徽猷，遹遵彝典，用圖治寧，咸有稱述。姑舉一二以實之：若漢武帝之罷黜百家、表章六經，光武之投戈講藝、息馬論道，唐太宗之《周禮》一書乙夜勤讀，固為美矣；其視堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武授受之心法，果何如哉？當時賢人君子出膺世用者，亦莫不獻忠效謀以匡乃辟：若董仲舒以經術顯，汲黯以忠鯁著，鄧禹立功名於光武，魏徵勸仁義於太宗，固可尚矣；其視臯、夔、伊、傅、周、召都俞密勿之事業，果何如哉？是以考論漢、唐君臣之治功，比之《詩》、《書》所稱則有所不及者，以其雜伯雜夷，徒有願治之名，而無躬行之實以為致理之本也。
恭惟陛下體二帝、三王之心，尊六經、孔子之道，監祖宗之成憲，以隆太平之治。心與道相涵，道與治相安，禮樂教化無非精神心術之著見，典章文物莫匪虛靈知覺之運行。是以四海乂安，萬邦協和，而躋斯世於熈皞者，是皆陛下夙夜匪遑、躬行之所致也。而又策臣以謹始圖
translation_en:
… is the most urgent. This is how Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) carried on the heritage of the past sages and inaugurated great peace for ten thousand generations.

Coming down to the Han and Tang dynasties and thereafter, there were no worthy and wise rulers who did not look up in admiration to those fine plans and follow the constant canons in order to seek orderly peace, and all of them had achievements worthy of praise. Let me cite one or two examples to substantiate this: Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi 漢武帝) dismissing the Hundred Schools and exalting the Six Classics; Emperor Guangwu (Guangwu 光武) laying down weapons to lecture on the arts and resting his horses to discuss the Way; and Emperor Taizong of Tang (Tang Taizong 唐太宗) diligently reading the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) late into the night—these were certainly admirable. Yet how do they truly compare with the method of the mind-and-heart transmitted and received by Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, Tang 湯, King Wen 文, and King Wu 武? In those times, among the worthy men and noble persons who came forth to serve the world, there were likewise none who did not offer loyalty and contribute counsel to assist their sovereigns: Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 became illustrious through classical scholarship, Ji An 汲黯 became renowned for his loyal outspokenness, Deng Yu 鄧禹 established merit and fame under Guangwu, and Wei Zheng 魏徵 urged benevolence and righteousness upon Taizong—these were certainly worthy of esteem. Yet how do they truly compare with the enterprises of harmonious counsel and assiduous devotion of Gao Yao 臯, Kui 夔, Yi Yin 伊, Fu Yue 傅, the Duke of Zhou 周, and the Duke of Shao 召? Therefore, when we examine and discuss the achievements in governance of the rulers and ministers of the Han and Tang, the reason they fall short compared to what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) and the Book of Documents (Shu 書) is that they were adulterated with the ways of hegemons and of barbarians, possessing merely the name of desiring good governance without the reality of personal practice to serve as the foundation for bringing about order.

Respectfully, I reflect that Your Majesty embodies the mind-and-heart of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, reveres the Way of the Six Classics and Confucius, and takes the established statutes of the Imperial Ancestors as a mirror so as to exalt the governance of great peace. Your mind-and-heart and the Way mutually permeate one another; the Way and governance rest securely together. Rites, music, and moral transformation are nothing other than the manifestation of your spiritual energy and mental art; institutions, statutes, and cultural forms are none other than the operation of your luminous, numinous awareness. Thus, that the Four Seas are settled in peace, the myriad states are brought into harmony, and this age is raised to a state of prosperous serenity—all of this has been brought about by Your Majesty's personal practice, without leisure morning or night. And yet You further question Your servant on how being careful at the beginning and planning for …

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
成必有其要推行之序必有其宜臣鄙陋不足
以上揆
淵衷臣聞敬者聖學之所以成始而成終者也謹
始圖成之要其在於此乎中庸凡為天下國家
有九經而脩身為首以及懷諸侯推行之序其
在於斯乎
陛下修己以敬其於謹始圖成而推行之者皆已行
之矣尚何詢於微臣哉然臣愚昧既以敷陳於
前矣謹於終篇竊有獻焉伏願
陛下始終此心始終此敬始終此治追虞周而比隆
===
陋漢唐而不居則
聖治神功超越前古斯民幸甚天下幸甚臣草茅微
賤荷蒙
教育其於致
君澤民之方固有志矣伏望
陛下俯垂采納臣不勝戰慄屏營之至臣謹對

punctuated: 成必有其要，推行之序必有其宜。臣鄙陋不足以上揆淵衷。臣聞敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也，謹始圖成之要，其在於此乎！《中庸》凡為天下國家有九經，而脩身為首，以及懷諸侯，推行之序，其在於斯乎！陛下修己以敬，其於謹始圖成而推行之者，皆已行之矣，尚何詢於微臣哉？然臣愚昧，既以敷陳於前矣，謹於終篇竊有獻焉：伏願陛下始終此心，始終此敬，始終此治，追虞、周而比隆，陋漢、唐而不居，則聖治神功超越前古，斯民幸甚，天下幸甚。臣草茅微賤，荷蒙教育，其於致君澤民之方，固有志矣。伏望陛下俯垂采納，臣不勝戰慄屏營之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: … completion must have its essential point, and the sequence of putting it into practice must have what is appropriate to it. Your servant is vulgar and shallow, and is unequal to fathoming the depths of Your Majesty's mind. Your servant has heard that reverence is that whereby sage learning brings about both the beginning and the completion; does the essential point of being careful at the beginning and planning for completion not lie in this? In the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), in all governance of the empire and the state there are nine standard rules, beginning with cultivating the person and extending to cherishing the feudal lords; does the sequence of putting it into practice not lie in this? Your Majesty cultivates Yourself with reverence; as for being careful at the beginning, planning for completion, and putting these into practice, You have already carried them all out—what need is there still to inquire of Your humble servant? Yet Your servant, ignorant and benighted, having already set forth his views above, respectfully ventures to offer a word at the conclusion of this essay: Your servant humbly prays that Your Majesty will from beginning to end maintain this mind, from beginning to end maintain this reverence, and from beginning to end maintain this governance, pursuing the eras of Yu and Zhou to rival their splendor, and disdaining Han and Tang as unworthy of dwelling in. Then Your sacred governance and divine achievements will surpass high antiquity; the people will be most fortunate, and the empire will be most fortunate. Your servant, of humble rustic origins, has been favored with Your nurturing education, and has truly long aspired to the means of bringing perfection to his Sovereign and blessings to the people. Your servant humbly hopes that Your Majesty will condescend to accept and adopt these words. Your servant is overcome with trembling and anxious awe. Your servant respectfully replies.

爰暨漢唐以來賢智之君莫不景仰徽猷適遵
彝典用圖治寧咸有稱述姑舉一二以實之若
漢武帝之罷黜百家表章六經光武之投戈講
藝息馬論道唐太宗之周禮一書乙夜勤讀固
為美矣其視堯舜禹湯文武授受之心法果何
如哉當時賢人君子出膺世用者亦莫不獻忠
效謀以匡乃辟若董仲舒以經術顯汲黯以忠
鯁著鄧禹立功名於光武魏徵勸仁義於太宗
固可尚矣其視皋夔伊傅周召都俞寮勿之事
業果何如哉是以考論漢唐君臣之治功比之
詩書所稱則有所不及者以其雜伯雜夷徒有
願治之名而無躬行之實以為致理之本也恭
惟
陛下體二帝三王之心尊六經孔子之道監
祖宗之成憲以隆太平之治心與道相涵道與治相
安禮樂教化無非精神心術之著見典章文物
莫匪虛靈知覺之運行是以四海又安萬邦協
和而躋斯世於熙皡者是皆
陛下夙夜匪遑躬行之所致也而又策臣以謹始圖
punctuated: 為急。此孔子所以繼承往聖，開萬世之太平也。爰暨漢、唐以来，賢智之君，莫不景仰徽猷，遹遵彝典，用圖治寧，咸有稱述。姑舉一二以實之：若漢武帝之罷黜百家，表章《六經》；光武之投戈講藝，息馬論道；唐太宗之《周禮》一書，乙夜勤讀，固為美矣。其視堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武授受之心法，果何如哉？當時賢人君子，出膺世用者，亦莫不獻忠效謀，以匡乃辟。若董仲舒以經術顯，汲黯以忠鯁著，鄧禹立功名於光武，魏徵勸仁義於太宗，固可尚矣。其視皋、夔、伊、傅、周、召都俞密勿之事業，果何如哉？是以考論漢、唐君臣之治功，比之《詩》、《書》所稱，則有所不及者，以其雜伯雜夷，徒有願治之名，而無躬行之實以為致理之本也。恭惟陛下，體二帝三王之心，尊《六經》、孔子之道，監祖宗之成憲，以隆太平之治。心與道相涵，道與治相安。禮樂教化，無非精神心術之著見；典章文物，莫匪虛靈知覺之運行。是以四海乂安，萬邦協和，而躋斯世於熈皡者，是皆陛下夙夜匪遑、躬行之所致也。而又策臣以謹始圖
translation_en: … as urgent. This is how Confucius succeeded the former sages and opened up great peace for ten thousand generations. Coming down to the Han and Tang dynasties and thereafter, wise and intelligent rulers without exception looked up with admiration to those fine plans and followed the constant canons in order to seek orderly peace, and all left things worthy of praise. Let me tentatively cite one or two examples to substantiate this: Emperor Wu of Han dismissing the Hundred Schools and exalting the Six Classics; Emperor Guangwu of Han casting aside his spear to lecture on the arts and resting his horses to discuss the Way; and Emperor Taizong of Tang diligently reading the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) late into the second watch of the night—these were certainly admirable. Yet compared with the method of the mind-and-heart (xinfa) transmitted and received by Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, how do they really measure up? In those times, worthy men and gentlemen who came forth to serve the world likewise never failed to offer their loyalty and contribute their counsels to assist their sovereigns. That Dong Zhongshu became illustrious through classical scholarship, Ji An became renowned for loyal outspokenness, Deng Yu established merit and fame under Guangwu, and Wei Zheng urged benevolence and righteousness upon Taizong—these are certainly worthy of esteem. Yet compared with the achievements of Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao in harmonious deliberation and earnest, confidential service, how do they really measure up? Therefore, when we examine and discuss the governing achievements of the rulers and ministers of the Han and Tang, the reason they fall short of what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) is that they mingled the ways of the霸 (hegemons) and the customs of the barbarians, possessing merely the name of desiring good governance without the reality of personal practice as the foundation for bringing about order. Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty embodies the minds of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, honors the Way of the Six Classics and Confucius, and takes as a mirror the established statutes of Your Imperial Ancestors so as to exalt the governance of great peace. Your mind and the Way mutually permeate one another; the Way and governance rest securely together. Rites, music, and moral transformation are nothing less than the manifestation of Your spiritual energy and mental cultivation; institutional canons and cultural forms are none other than the operation of Your clear, numinous awareness. Thus, that the Four Seas are well-governed and at peace, the myriad states are in harmony, and this age is raised to prosperous tranquility—all this has been brought about by Your Majesty's personal practice, allowing Yourself no leisure morning or night. And yet You further question Your servant in this policy examination on how to be cautious at the beginning and plan for …

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
成必有其要推行之序必有其宜臣鄙陋不足
以上揆
淵衷臣聞敬者聖學之所以成始而成終者也謹
始圖成之要其在於此乎中庸凡為天下國家
有九經而脩身為首以及懷諸侯推行之序其
在於斯乎
陛下修已以敬其於謹始圖成而推行之者皆已行
之矣尚何詢於微臣哉然臣愚昧既以敷陳於
前矣謹於終篇竊有獻焉伏願
陛下始終此心始終此敬始終此治追虞周而比隆
===

聖治神功超越前古斯民幸甚天下幸甚臣草茅微

教育其於致
君澤民之方固有志矣伏望

賤荷蒙

punctuated: 成，必有其要，推行之序，必有其宜。臣鄙陋，不足以上揆淵衷。臣聞敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。謹始圖成之要，其在於此乎？《中庸》凡為天下國家有九經，而脩身為首，以及懷諸侯，推行之序，其在於斯乎？陛下修已以敬，其於謹始圖成而推行之者，皆已行之矣，尚何詢於微臣哉？然臣愚昧，既以敷陳於前矣，謹於終篇，竊有獻焉。伏願陛下始終此心，始終此敬，始終此治，追虞、周而比隆，陋漢、唐而不居，則聖治神功超越前古，斯民幸甚，天下幸甚。臣草茅微賤，荷蒙教育，其於致君澤民之方，固有志矣。伏望陛下俯垂采納，臣不勝戰慄屏營之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: … the outcome, there must be an essential key; and for the sequence of putting it into practice, there must be an appropriate order. Your servant is rustic and shallow, unworthy of fathoming the depths of Your Imperial thoughts. Yet your servant has heard that reverence is that by which the learning of the sages completes both the beginning and the end. Does the essential key to being cautious at the beginning and planning for the outcome not lie here? According to the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), in all governance of the empire and the state there are nine standard rules, beginning with cultivating the person and extending to cherishing the feudal lords; does the sequence of putting it into practice not lie in this? Your Majesty cultivates yourself with reverence; as for being cautious at the beginning, planning for the outcome, and putting them into practice, You have already carried them all out—why then should You still inquire of this humble servant? Nevertheless, ignorant as your servant is, having already set forth my views above, I respectfully presume to offer a final word at the close of this essay. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will maintain this mind from beginning to end, maintain this reverence from beginning to end, and maintain this governance from beginning to end—emulating Yu and Zhou so as to rival their prosperity, while disdaining Han and Tang and refusing to rest at their level. Then Your sacred governance and divine achievements will surpass those of antiquity; how fortunate for this people, how fortunate for all under Heaven! Coming from the rustic grass and of lowly station, your servant has been favored with imperial education, and has long cherished the aspiration to assist my Sovereign and benefit the people. I humbly hope that Your Majesty will condescend to select and adopt my words. Your servant is overcome with the utmost trembling and anxious awe. Your servant respectfully replies.

正統四年進士登科錄

玉音

正統四年閏二月二十六日早，行在禮部尚書臣胡濙等官於奉天門奏：為科舉事。會試天下舉人，選中一百名。本年三月初二日殿試，合請讀卷及執事等官少師、工部尚書兼謹身殿大學士楊榮，少保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士楊溥等三十八員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。欽此。」

光祿大夫、柱國、少師、工部尚書兼謹身殿大學士楊榮〔庚辰進士〕
translation_en:
Record of the Metropolitan Graduates of the Fourth Year of the Zhengtong Era [1439]

Imperial Decree

Early on the twenty-sixth day of the intercalary second month of the fourth year of the Zhengtong era [April 9, 1439], Your servant Hu Ying 胡濙, Minister of Rites in the Auxiliary Administration at the Imperial Sojourn, and other officials memorialized at the Gate of Worshipping Heaven (Fengtianmen) concerning the civil service examinations: "In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from across the realm, one hundred men have been selected. For the Palace Examination on the second day of the third month of this year [April 15, 1439], it is fitting to request thirty-eight officials to serve as Readers of Examination Papers and functionaries, including Yang Rong 楊榮, Junior Preceptor, Minister of Works, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving the Person (Jinshendian), and Yang Pu 楊溥, Junior Guardian, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory (Wuyingdian). Regarding the ranks and statuses conferred upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi), we respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi): in the First Class, by precedent three men are selected, the first ranked as従6 [Rank 6b] and the second and third ranked as正7 [Rank 7a], all granted the title 'Metropolitan Graduate with Honors' (jinshi jidi); those in the Second Class are ranked as従7 [Rank 7b] and granted the title 'Metropolitan Graduate' (jinshi chushen); those in the Third Class are ranked as正8 [Rank 8a] and granted the title 'Associate Metropolitan Graduate' (tong jinshi chushen)." We received the Imperial Edict: "Approved. Respect this."

Readers of Examination Papers

Yang Rong 楊榮, Grandee of the Thirty-eighth Class (guanglu dafu), Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor, Minister of Works, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving the Person (a metropolitan graduate of the gengchen year [1400]).

三月初二日早，諸貢士赴內府殿試，上御奉天殿，親賜策問。
三月初四日早，文武百官朝服侍班。是日，行在錦衣衛設鹵簿于丹陛、丹墀內，上御奉天殿，行在鴻臚寺官傳制唱名。行在禮部官捧黃榜，鼓樂導引，出長安左門外張掛。畢，順天府官用傘盖、儀從送状元歸第。
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors

Fourth year of the Zhengtong reign (1439)

Early on the second day of the third month, the Tribute Scholars proceeded to the Inner Palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty took his seat in the Hall of Heaven's Mandate (Fengtian dian) and personally bestowed the policy question.

Early on the fourth day of the third month, all civil and military officials stood in attendance in court dress. On this day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard of the Auxiliary Administration set up the imperial insignia arrays upon the Cinnabar Steps and within the Cinnabar Courtyard. His Majesty took his seat in the Hall of Heaven's Mandate, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial of the Auxiliary Administration transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names on the roll. Officials of the Ministry of Rites of the Auxiliary Administration carried the Yellow Placard, led by drums and music, out beyond the Left Chang'an Gate to post it on display. Once this was completed, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the Principal Graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols and a ceremonial retinue.

translation_en:
On the fifth day of the third month, the Principal Graduate (zhuangyuan) was bestowed court robes, a cap, and a belt, and a banquet was bestowed at the Auxiliary Ministry of Rites. After the banquet concluded, they proceeded to the Auxiliary Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.

On the sixth day of the third month, the Principal Graduate led all the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) in submitting a memorial to express gratitude for Imperial grace.

On the seventh day of the third month, all the metropolitan graduates went to the Temple of the First Teacher Confucius to perform the ritual offering of vegetables (shicai). The Auxiliary Ministry of Rites memorialized to request that the Auxiliary Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele inscribed with their names at the Directorate of Education in Beijing.

第一甲三名，賜進士及第。

施槃〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治《春秋》，字宗銘，行一，年二十三，二月十三日生〕。曾祖希敬，祖志方，父遵道，母金氏，繼母嚴氏。具慶下。弟宗賢。娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第十五名，會試第五十五名。

楊鼎〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字宗器，行一，年三十一，五月二十五日生〕。曾祖伯安，祖惟敬，父森，母劉氏，繼母李氏。具慶下。弟鼒。未娶。陝西鄉試第一名，會試第一名。

倪謙〔貫應天府上元縣，匠籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字克讓，行二，年二十五，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖公起，祖德潤，父子安，母屠氏，繼母孫氏。重慶下。兄誠。聘姚氏。應天府鄉試第五十四名，會試第七十八名。
translation_en:
First Class, three candidates, conferred the degree of Metropolitan Graduate with Honors (jinshi jidi).

Shi Pan 施槃 [registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Directly Attached (Zhili), under a civilian household registration; an Added Student of the County School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Zongming, first in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Xijing; his grandfather was Zhifang; his father is Zundao; his mother was Lady Jin; and his stepmother is Lady Yan. Both his father and stepmother are living. His younger brother is Zongxian. He married Lady Wu. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ding 楊鼎 [registered in Xianning County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, under a civilian household registration; a National University Student (guozisheng) specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zongqi, first in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Bo'an; his grandfather was Weijing; his father is Sen; his mother was Lady Liu; and his stepmother is Lady Li. Both his father and stepmother are living. His younger brother is Zi 鼒. He is unmarried. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Qian 倪謙 [registered in Shangyuan County, Yingtian Prefecture, under an artisan household registration; a Student of the Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Kerang, second in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-five, born on the first day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Gongqi; his grandfather is Derun; his father is Zi'an; his mother was Lady Tu; and his stepmother is Lady Sun. Both his grandparents and his parents are living. His elder brother is Cheng. He is betrothed to Lady Yao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class, thirty-five candidates, conferred the status of Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi chushen):

Zhang He 張和 (registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili], under a civilian household; an Added Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of History [Shujing]; courtesy name Jiezhi 節之; second in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Daosheng 道昇, his grandfather was Wenyu 文裕, his father is Yongli 用禮, and his mother is née He 何. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Zhen 禎, and his younger brothers are Mu 穆 (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination) and Zhong 种. He is married to née Ding 丁. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Pu 錢溥 (registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili], under a civilian household; an Added Student of the Prefectural School; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals [Chunqiu]; courtesy name Yuanpu 原溥; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Deyu 德玉, his grandfather was Huazhong 華仲, his father is Weiqing 惟慶, and his mother is née Zhao 趙. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Yuanbo 原博. He is married to née Zhuang 莊. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lun 章綸 (registered in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under a military household; a Student of the Prefectural School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Dajing 大經; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the sixth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Xing 性, his grandfather was Xinmin 新民, his father was Wenbao 文寶, his mother was née Jin 金, and his stepmother is née Bao 包. His mother is living and his father is deceased. His elder brothers are You 𧫎, Yan 琰, and Qian 嵌, and his younger brother is Sui 嵗. He is betrothed to née Zhu 朱. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fu 劉孚 (registered as a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; a student in the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; courtesy name Chengzhi 誠之; first in seniority among his brothers; forty-five years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month). His younger brother is Zaizhi 載之, and he is married to née Xiao 蕭氏. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Hao 祝顥 (registered as a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili]; a student in the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes; courtesy name Weiqing 維清; third in seniority among his brothers; thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Zhu Ziqian 子潛, his grandfather was Zhu Jingzhang 景章, his father was Zhu Huanwen 煥文, and his mother is née Wang 王氏. His mother is living. His elder brother is Weide 維德, and he is married to née Qian 錢氏. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Sui 夏遂 (registered as a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili]; an expectant student of the secondary quota in the county school specializing in the Record of Rites; courtesy name Cunliang 存良; fourth in seniority among his brothers; twenty-two years old, born on the thirteenth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Xia Wenda 文達, his grandfather was Xia Youliang 友諒, his father was Xia Shanzhang 善長, and his mother is née Lin 林氏. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Xia You 佑 (former Assistant Magistrate of Linhai County), Xia Fu 輔, and Xia Xian 顯, and he is betrothed to née Liang 梁氏. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Feng 李鳳 (registered as a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; a student in the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; courtesy name Chaoyang 朝陽; third in seniority among his brothers; twenty-six years old, born on the tenth day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Li Borou 伯柔 (Department Magistrate of Qinzhou under the Yuan), his grandfather was Li Yanheng 彦亨 (Director of Instruction in the Establishment of the Prince of Xiang), his father is Li Xiaohuo 肖穫, and his mother was née Wang 王氏. His father is living. His elder brothers are Li Yingxiang 應祥 and Li Yingwen 應文, and he is betrothed to née Wang 王氏. His elder brother is Chen Fu, and his younger brothers are Chen Ding, Chen Tai, Chen Yu, Chen Qian, Chen Xian, and Chen Heng. He is married to Lady Lin. He placed twenty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xun 張勛: Registered in a military household in Huining County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi; a County School Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Yiding, first in generational order among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang Weizhao, his grandfather Zhang Zhong, his father Zhang Yongfu, and his mother Lady Wang. Both of his parents are living. He is married to Lady Xian. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Chen 黃琛: Registered in a civilian household in Jiangle County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Tingxian, first in generational order among his brothers, aged twenty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Huang Zishi, his grandfather Huang Gonggui, his father Huang Chong, and his mother Lady Xiao. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Huang Zan. He is betrothed to Lady Chen. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan 張瓛: Registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a County School Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Weijing, second in generational order among his brothers, aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang Rongfu, his grandfather Zhang Bocheng, his father Zhang Zhongfang, and his mother Lady Sun. His mother is living. His elder brother is Zhang Bingyi. He is married to Lady Shen. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉彧〔貫山東青州府益都縣軍籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字著章，行一，年三十八，八月十八日生〕。曾祖彥成，祖遵道，父公弼，母孫氏。重慶下，弟忠、鼎、政，娶陳氏。山東鄉試第二十六名，會試第三十四名。

孟玘〔貫福建福州府閩縣軍籍，府學增廣生，治《書經》，字廷振，行六，年二十八，正月十八日生〕。曾祖良〔元鉛砲夫百戶〕，祖德〔元浙東元帥〕，父文，母葉氏。具慶下，弟瑞，娶張氏。福建鄉試第六名，會試第十名。

張穆〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《書經》，字敬之，行三，年二十五，十二月二十五日生〕。曾祖道昇，祖文裕，父用禮，母何氏。具慶下，兄稹、和〔同科進士〕，弟种，娶周氏。應天府鄉試第四十二名，會試第二名。

周賢〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，府學生，治《易經》，字用希，行三，年三十三，三月十三日生〕。曾祖貴五，祖成一，父彥達，母陸氏。具慶下，兄用明，弟能，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第十二名，會試第六十四名。
translation_en:
Liu Yu 劉彧 (registered under a military household in Yidu County 益都縣, Qingzhou Prefecture 青州府, Shandong 山東; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Documents [Shujing]; courtesy name Zhuzhang 著章; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Liu Yancheng 彥成, his grandfather was Liu Zundao 遵道, his father is Liu Gongbi 公弼, and his mother is Lady Sun 孫氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living; his younger brothers are Zhong 忠, Ding 鼎, and Zheng 政; he is married to Lady Chen 陳氏. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Qi 孟玘 (registered under a military household in Min County 閩縣, Fuzhou Prefecture 福州府, Fujian 福建; an Added Student of the Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Documents [Shujing]; courtesy name Tingzhen 廷振; sixth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Meng Liang 良 (Commander of a Hundred Lead-Cannon Men under the Yuan), his grandfather was Meng De 德 (Regional Commander of Zhedong under the Yuan), his father is Meng Wen 文, and his mother is Lady Ye 葉氏. Both his parents are living; his younger brother is Rui 瑞; he is married to Lady Zhang 張氏. He ranked sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mu 張穆 (registered under a civilian household in Kunshan County 崑山縣, Suzhou Prefecture 蘇州府, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili 直隸]; an Added Student of the County School specializing in the Classic of Documents [Shujing]; courtesy name Jingzhi 敬之; third in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Zhang Daosheng 道昇, his grandfather was Zhang Wenyu 文裕, his father is Zhang Yongli 用禮, and his mother is Lady He 何氏. Both his parents are living; his elder brothers are Zhen 稹 and He 和 (a metropolitan graduate [jinshi] of the same examination class), and his younger brother is Chong 种; he is married to Lady Zhou 周氏. He ranked forty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture 應天府 Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xian 周賢 (registered under a civilian household in Changzhou County 長洲縣, Suzhou Prefecture 蘇州府, Southern Metropolitan Area [Zhili 直隸]; a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Yongxi 用希; third in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Zhou Guiwu 貴五, his grandfather was Zhou Chengyi 成一, his father is Zhou Yanda 彥達, and his mother is Lady Lu 陸氏. Both his parents are living; his elder brother is Yongming 用明 and his younger brother is Neng 能; he is married to Lady Chen 陳氏. He ranked twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture 應天府 Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

甘敬脩〔貫四川叙州府富順縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字士勉，行二，年三十八，八月二十九日生〕。曾祖壽；祖志高；父雨；母施氏。具慶下。兄敬儒；弟敬身。娶姜氏。四川鄉試第十八名，會試第二十三名。

translation_en:
Zhou Tianmin 周天民 (registered as a civilian household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan; a County School Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Xiyin, second in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Zhou Deng; his grandfather was Zhou Gui; his father is Zhou Shaojing; his mother was Lady Zhang, and his stepmother is Lady Huang. Both parents are living (father and stepmother). His elder brother is Tianxiang, and his younger brothers are Zhen and Yu. He married Lady Chen. He ranked eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhang 王彰 (registered as a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong; a Prefectural School Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals [Chunqiu]; courtesy name Tingxian, third in seniority among brothers, aged forty-five, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Wang Zhizheng; his grandfather was Wang Renqing; his father was Wang Wenkai; his mother was Lady Chen. Both parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Dong and Bin, and his younger brother is Mei. He married Lady Du, and remarried Lady Lin. He ranked first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gan Jingxiu 甘敬脩 (registered as a military household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan; an Expectant-Quota County School Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Shimian, second in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Gan Shou; his grandfather was Gan Zhigao; his father is Gan Yu; his mother is Lady Shi. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Jingru, and his younger brother is Jingshen. He married Lady Jiang. He ranked eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Cong 林聰 (registered as a civilian household in Ningde County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a County School Student specializing in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Jicong, fifth in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Lin Xu; his grandfather was Lin Yanzhao (Assistant County Magistrate of Pingshan County); his father is Lin Guan (retired Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Jiangshan County); his legal mother is Lady Ni, and his birth mother is Lady Chen. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Boshao, Zhongfu, Shumian, and Jicheng. He married Lady Tang. He ranked ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Tang 張瑭 [native of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, of civilian registration, an Added Student in the county Confucian school, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), courtesy name Tingyu, ninth in family seniority, age twenty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Lühe; his grandfather is Zongchun; his father is Cheng; his mother is née Chen. Both his parents and grandparents are living. His elder brothers are Zhen and Yu, and his younger brothers are Xu, Yu, Yuan, Bin, Xiang, Qi, and Shan. He married née Ye. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Qian 殷謙 [native of Zhuo Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, of civilian registration, an Added Student in the subprefectural Confucian school, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), courtesy name Wenhui, third in family seniority, age twenty-three, born on the first day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Liangfu; his grandfather was Kegong; his father is Li [serving as Instructor of the Confucian School of Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi]; his mother is née Lu. Both his parents are living. His elder brothers are Gang and Rang. He married née Wang. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xuan 楊璿 [native of Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), of military registration, an Added Student in the county Confucian school, specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), courtesy name Shuji, seventh in family seniority, age twenty-four, born on the ninth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Guang; his grandfather was Yuanzhen; his father was Zongyuan; his mother is née Zhu. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Shuchun, Shuzhang, Shuheng, and Shuying, and his younger brother is Shuzhen. He is betrothed to née Tang. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Duo 俞鐸 [native of Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, of civilian registration, a Student in the county Confucian school, specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing), courtesy name Zhenwen, second in family seniority, age twenty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Benchu [Assistant Magistrate of Yingdao County]; his grandfather was Yanyong; his father is Shuhui; his mother was née Dong, and his stepmother is née Ding. Both his father and stepmother are living. His elder brother is Luan, and his younger brothers are Fu, Qin, and Ling. He married née Chen. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

王宇〔貫河南開封府祥符縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治《書經》，字仲宏，行四，年二十三，閏五月初四日生〕。曾祖敦本，祖友德，父希哲，母丁氏。慈侍下，兄仲和、仲玉、仲儀，弟宜宗，聘段氏。河南鄉試第一名，會試第八名。

translation_en:
Luo Ying 羅瑛 (native of Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, of civilian registration; an added student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Qingqing, fourth in seniority among brothers, aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Hongdao, his grandfather was Jingfu, his father is Huaiyu, and his mother is née Xu. Both parents are living; his elder brothers are Hu (serving as Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Shucheng County), Jin, and Shen; his younger brothers are Zu, Gang, and Chun; and he is married to née Xiong. He ranked seventy-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jian 王儉 (native of Tongliang County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, of civilian registration; a student at the Badong County school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Yongjie, fourth in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather was Shengzong, his father was Zhongheng, and his mother is née Guo. His mother is living; his elder brothers are Gang (serving as Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Badong County), Zuo, and You; his younger brothers are Kan, Wei, Ru, Xiu, and Yi; and he is married to née Ma. He ranked nineteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yu 王宇 (native of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, of military registration; an added student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Zhonghong, fourth in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-three, born on the fourth day of the intercalary fifth month). His great-grandfather was Dunben, his grandfather was Youde, his father was Xizhe, and his mother is née Ding. His mother is living; his elder brothers are Zhonghe, Zhongyu, and Zhongyi; his younger brother is Yizong; and he is betrothed to née Duan. He ranked first in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mian 張勉 (native of Ying Subprefecture, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, of military registration; an added student at the Liaocheng County school specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Keqin, first in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-five, born on the seventh day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Junmei, his grandfather was Rong (District Magistrate of Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture), his father is Wenxian (former Postal Relay Station Master of Changqing), and his mother is née Liu. Both parents are living, and he is married to née Zhao. He ranked eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

章繪〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，順天府富戶，儒士，治《禮記》，字尚素，行五，年二十四，十月十五日生〕。曾祖義春；祖禮榮；父智通；母俞氏。慈侍下。兄維、經、綸、純；弟紹。娶張氏。順天府鄉試第三十三名，會試第十一名。

王竑〔貫湖廣武昌府江夏縣軍籍，河州衛學軍生，治《禮記》，字公度，行三，年二十六，六月二十日生〕。曾祖景〔元水軍翼萬戶〕；祖俊卿〔福州右衛百戶〕；父佐；母周氏。具慶下。兄竣、靖。娶孫氏。陝西鄉試第四名，會試第五名。

尚達〔貫山東兖州府東平州軍籍，州學生，治《書經》，字兼善，行一，年三十八，十一月十六日生〕。曾祖添祐；祖名遠；父思忠；母劉氏。重慶下。弟遴、遜。娶樊氏。山東鄉試第一名，會試第二十八名。
translation_en:
Zhang Hui 章繪 [registered as a civilian householder of Yin County 鄞縣, Ningbo Prefecture 寧波府, Zhejiang 浙江, and a wealthy householder (fuhu) in Shuntian Prefecture 順天府; a Confucian scholar (rushi) specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Shangsu 尚素; fifth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-four sui, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Yichun 義春; his grandfather was Lirong 禮榮; his father was Zhitong 智通; his mother is née Yu 俞氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased (cishi xia). His elder brothers are Wei 維, Jing 經, Lun 綸, and Chun 純; his younger brother is Shao 紹. He is married to née Zhang 張氏. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ou Wenzheng 歐文整 [registered as a civilian householder of Mei Subprefecture 眉州, Sichuan 四川; a Subprefectural Student (zhou xuesheng) specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zhengzong 正宗; third in seniority among his brothers; aged forty sui, born on the eleventh day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Miaozheng 妙政; his grandfather was Junxiu 均秀; his father was Mengxian 孟賢; his mother was née Tian 田氏. Both his parents are deceased (yonggan xia). His elder brothers are Wencong 文聰 and Wenzhi 文質. He is married to née Zhou 周氏. He placed twenty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hong 王竑 [registered in a military household of Jiangxia County 江夏縣, Wuchang Prefecture 武昌府, Huguang 湖廣; a Military Student (junsheng) of the Hezhou Guard Confucian School (Hezhou weixue 河州衛學), specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Gongdu 公度; third in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-six sui, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Jing 景 [Brigade Commander of a Naval Wing (shuijun yi wanhu) under the Yuan dynasty]; his grandfather was Junqing 俊卿 [Company Commander (baihu) of the Fuzhou Right Guard (Fuzhou youwei 福州右衛)]; his father is Zuo 佐; his mother is née Zhou 周氏. Both his parents are living (juqing xia). His elder brothers are Jun 竣 and Jing 靖. He is married to née Sun 孫氏. He placed fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Da 尚達 [registered in a military household of Dongping Subprefecture 東平州, Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府, Shandong 山東; a Subprefectural Student (zhou xuesheng) specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Jianshan 兼善; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-eight sui, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Tianyou 添祐; his grandfather is Mingyuan 名遠; his father is Sizhong 思忠; his mother is née Liu 劉氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living (chongqing xia). His younger brothers are Lin 遴 and Xun 遜. He is married to née Fan 樊氏. He placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉煒〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣民籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字有融，行二十四，年三十一，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖正可；祖珝〔鄉貢士〕；父惟繁；母錢氏。具慶下。兄焲；弟熈、炳。娶毛氏。浙江鄉試第三十八名，會試第四十二名。
translation_en:
Feng Qing 豐慶 [registered in a civilian household of Ruichang County 瑞昌縣, Jiujiang Prefecture 九江府, Jiangxi 江西; Added Student (zengguang sheng) of the Prefectural School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name [omitted]; age twenty-seven; born on the ninth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Feng Maosi 豐茂四; his grandfather was Feng Renyi 豐仁一; his father was Feng Chu 豐初 [Instructor (jiaoyu) of the Dehua County 德化縣 School]; his mother is née Teng 滕氏. His mother is living (cishi xia). His elder brothers are Feng Shou 豐壽 and Feng Zong 豐宗. He married née Bao 鮑氏, and married as his second wife née Shi 史氏. He ranked sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Ying 孟瑛 [registered in a military household of the Guide Guard 歸德衛, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸); Military Student (junsheng) of the Guide Subprefectural 歸德州 School; specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Yanhui 彦輝; first in seniority among brothers; age twenty-four; born on the fifth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Meng Lin 孟林; his grandfather was Meng Rong 孟榮; his father is Meng Jing 孟景; his legal mother is née Gao 高氏, and his birth mother is née Liu 劉氏. Both parents are living (juqing xia). His younger brothers are Meng Jin 孟瑾 and Meng Xuan 孟瑄. He married née Li 李氏. He ranked fifteenth in the Henan 河南 Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Tang 姚堂 [registered in a civilian household of Cixi County 慈谿縣, Ningbo Prefecture 寧波府, Zhejiang 浙江; Added Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Yanrong 彦容; ninth in seniority; age twenty-three; born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Yao Juxun 姚居遜; his grandfather was Yao Minguan 姚敏觀; his father is Yao Yu 姚愚; his mother is née Jiang 姜氏. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Yao Xun 姚塤, Yao Lei 姚壘, Yao Bi 姚璧, and Yao Xun 姚壎. He married née Yang 楊氏. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Wei 劉煒 [registered in a civilian household of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang; Student (xuesheng) of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Yourong 有融; twenty-fourth in seniority; age thirty-one; born on the ninth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Zhengke 劉正可; his grandfather was Liu Xu 劉珝 [Tribute Student from the Provinces (xiang gongshi)]; his father is Liu Weifan 劉惟繁; his mother is née Qian 錢氏. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Liu Yi 劉焲; his younger brothers are Liu Xi 劉熈 and Liu Bing 劉炳. He married née Mao 毛氏. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Tier, sixty-one men, conferred the status of Fellow of the Metropolitan Graduates (tong jinshi chushen).

Mo Zhen 莫震 [registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), under military household status; a County Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Tingwei, third in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Mo Shi, his grandfather was Mo Xili, his father is Mo Yuan, and his mother is née Shen. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Mo Yun and Mo Lin, and he is married to née Pan. He placed fifty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Gan 鄒榦 [registered in Yuhang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian household status; a Prefectural Student of Yingtian Prefecture specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zongsheng, second in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the seventh month]. His great-grandfather was Zou Changsi, his grandfather was Zou Fujian, his father was Zou Ji [Vice Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent (Zhanshifu Shaozhanshi), posthumously promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Taizi Shaobao), and canonized as Wenmin], and his mother was née Xue. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Zou Ben, and he is married to née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Gongchen 胡拱辰 [registered in Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian household status; an Added Student of the Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Gongzhi, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-three, born on the first day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Hu Daochang, his grandfather was Hu Zhiliang, his father is Hu Ze [retired Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Yongfeng County, Jiangxi], his legal mother is née Wu, and his birth mother is née Zhou. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Hu Gongbi, and he is betrothed to née Lin. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mao Feng 毛鳳 [registered as a commoner in Jiajiang County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); style name Caifeng; second in seniority among his brothers; age forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month]. His great-grandfather was Mao Shangxian, his grandfather was Mao Wengui, his father was Mao Youzhi, and his mother is Madam Fu. His mother is living (his father having passed away). He has an elder brother, Zhongxian, and younger brothers, Zhongcong, Zhonggang, and Zhong'an; he is married to Madam Chen. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Kun 呂困 [registered in an artisan household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a County Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Xiyan; third in seniority among his brothers; age twenty-two, born on the second day of the second lunar month]. His great-grandfather was Lü Maozhi, his grandfather was Lü Mingde, his father was Lü Zongjing, and his mother is Madam Lu. His mother is living (his father having passed away). He is married to Madam Wang. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefectural (Provincial) Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rong 李榮 [registered as a commoner in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; an Added Student of the Prefectural School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Zhiren; fourth in seniority among his brothers; age twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month]. His great-grandfather was Li Ming, his grandfather is Li Pi, his father is Li Ji, and his mother is Madam Lin. Both his parents and grandparents are living. He has younger brothers, Hua, Fu, Gui, Ju, and Ju; he is married to Madam Chen. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Han 劉澣 [registered in a military household in Gong County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Zixin; fourth in seniority among his brothers; age forty, born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Daoyan, his grandfather was Liu Yungong, his father was Liu Zhonghua, his mother was Madam Liao, and his stepmother was Madam Xiang. Both his parents are deceased. He has elder brothers, Zicong [Instructor in the Prefectural/County School of Divination (Yinyang xue xunshu) of the same county], Zixing, and Zigao, and a younger brother, Zibin; he married Madam Tang and was subsequently betrothed to Madam Yan. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Liu Wang 旺; his grandfather was Liu Wenyi 文義; his father is Liu Qing 清 [formerly Right Assistant Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial in the Auxiliary Administration at the Secondary Capital]; his mother is Lady Zhang 張氏. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Liu Yu 昱, and he is married to Lady Wang 王氏. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jing 馬經 [registered in an artisan household in Dongguang County 東光縣, Jing Department 景州, Hejian Prefecture 河間府, Zhili 直隸; a student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Yongchang 用常; first in seniority among brothers; age thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month]. His great-grandfather was Ma Dezhao 德昭; his grandfather is Ma Shiyuan 視遠 [Secretary in the Ministry of Works]; his father is Ma Anru 闇如; his legal mother is Lady Li 李氏; his birth mother is Lady Bao 鮑氏. Both grandparents and parents are living. His younger brothers are Ma Lun 綸, Ma Gang 綱, and Ma Ji 紀, and he is married to Lady Xu 徐氏. He placed seventh in the Yunnan 雲南 Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yue 張鉞 [registered in a military household in Xin'an County 新安縣, Henan Prefecture 河南府, Henan 河南; a prefectural Confucian school student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Daqi 大器; third in seniority among brothers; age thirty, born on the first day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Si 思; his grandfather was Zhang Shizhong 時中; his father was Zhang Yue 嶽 [Assistant Magistrate of Xiangyuan County 襄垣縣, Shanxi 山西]; his mother is Lady Shan 單氏. His mother is living (his father having died). His elder brothers are Zhang Zhao 釗 and Zhang Zhu 鑄, and he is married to Lady Ning 寧氏. He placed twenty-second in the Henan 河南 Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hu 汪滸 [registered in an official household in Cheng County 成縣, Gongchang Prefecture 鞏昌府, Shaanxi 陝西; a student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Qingfu 清夫; fourth in seniority among brothers; age thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Youcai 友才 [Overseer (Darughachi) of Jin Department 金州 under the Yuan dynasty]; his grandfather was Wang Dezhong 德中 [Assistant Department Magistrate of Zhao Department 趙州]; his father was Wang Zongxian 宗賢 [Assistant Prefect of Songjiang Prefecture 松江府]; his mother is Lady Wu 武氏. His mother is living (his father having died). His elder brothers are Wang Jun 濬, Wang Pu 溥, and Wang Hao 浩; his elder paternal cousin is Wang Shou 壽 [Vice Commander of the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission]; his younger brothers are Wang Lan 瀾 and Wang Shu 澍, and he is married to Lady Rui 芮氏. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi 陝西 Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.
