translation_en:
Chen Jia 陳价 (registered in Tongliang County, He Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, under artisan household status; a subprefectural student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Weifan, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month). His great-grandfather was Chen Wenming, his grandfather was Chen Zhixian, his father is Chen Yu, and his mother is née Bao. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Chen Qiao, Chen Ti, Chen Lun, Chen Zhuo, Chen You, and Chen Xiu. He is married to née Feng. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hao 周濠 (registered in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, under civilian household status; an expectant student of the county school specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Wenyuan, third in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Zhou Nansi, his grandfather was Zhou Shurong, his father is Zhou Yanyu, and his mother is née Xiang. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Zhou Wei and Zhou Yong. He is married to née Wang. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xu 劉珝 (registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, under Confucian scholar household status; a county student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Qiusu, eleventh in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Liu Yanchang, his grandfather was Liu Ziding, his father was Liu Zhiqing, and his mother is née Luo. His mother is living. His elder brother is Liu Pu, and his paternal cousin is Liu Qiu (Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy). He is married to née Gao. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tai 李泰 (registered in Tancheng County, Yi Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, under civilian household status; an expectant student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Yudao, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-six, born on the first day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Li Juxing (posthumously honoured as Gentleman for Literature and Investigating Censor of the Guizhou Circuit), his grandfather is Li Ji (invested as Grand Master of Palace Accord and Prefect of Henan Prefecture), his father is Li Lin (Instructor of the Changyuan County School), his grandmother is née Liu (ennobled as Lady of Suitability), and his mother is née Bao. Both his grandparents and parents are living. His younger brother is Li Xingbang. He is married to née Zhao. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Fang 劉芳 [registered in Cangxi County 蒼溪縣, Baoning Prefecture 保寧府, Sichuan 四川, in a civilian household; a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); style name Yongxing 永馨; third in seniority among his brothers; age thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Zhicong 智聡; his grandfather was Wenguang 文廣; his father is Zhongcai 仲才, and his mother is née Pu 蒲. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Duan 端, Zheng 正, and Bin 斌, and his younger brother is Zhen 珍. He married née Huang 黃. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Ying 楊瑛 [registered in Putian County 莆田縣, Xinghua Prefecture 興化府, Fujian 福建, in a civilian household; a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); style name Dehua 德華; seventy-first in seniority in his generation; age thirty-one, born on the fourth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Yuanji 原吉; his grandfather was Kongyin 孔殷 [Prefectural Physician in the Medical School of this prefecture]; his father is Tai 泰, and his mother is née Xu 許. Both parents are living. He married née Xu 許. He placed twenty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Zicong 何子聰 [registered in Wuqiao County 吳橋縣, Jing Department 景州, Hejian Prefecture 河間府, Zhili 直隸, in a civilian household; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); style name Youwen 友聞; second in seniority among his brothers; age thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Yanzhong 彥中; his grandfather is Kejing 克敬; his father is Fuyuan 福原 [County Instructor in the Yin-Yang School], and his mother is née Li 李. Both parents and grandparents are living. His elder brother is Kuan 寛, and his younger brothers are Zi'an 子安, Zirong 子榮, Zining 子寧, and Zizhi 子智. He married née Zhang 張. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nie Zhi 聶智 [registered in Fengcheng County 豐城縣, Nanchang Prefecture 南昌府, Jiangxi 江西, in a civilian household; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Zhijie 志節; fourth in seniority among his brothers; age forty-four, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Longying 隆膺; his grandfather was Zisheng 子勝; his father was Konghui 孔惠, and his mother is née Xu 徐. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Yanjie 彥節, Changjie 常節, and Youjie 有節, and his younger brothers are Kangjie 康節, Yongjie 用節, Ningjie 寧節, and Hongjie 弘節. He married née Yang 楊. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

秦中〔貫陝西鳳翔府鳳翔縣，民籍，府學生，治《書經》，字時中，行二，年三十一，三月二十二日生〕。曾祖彥賓，祖成，父允哲，母李氏。具慶下。兄荆玉。娶潘氏。陝西郷試第六名，會試第六十八名。
translation_en:
Jiao Kuan 焦寛 [native of Ye County, Yu Subprefecture, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, of civilian registration, a County Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), courtesy name Zhongrong, fourth in seniority, aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Jiao Cheng; his grandfather was Jiao Jing; his father was Jiao Ying [Assistant Magistrate of Pingxiang County, Jiangxi, posthumously honored as Investigating Censor of the Guangdong Circuit]; and his mother was née Geng [posthumously honored as Child Nurturer]. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Jiao Ning, Jiao Hong [Right Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi], and Jiao Yi. He married née Ma. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shan Yu 單宇 [native of Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, of civilian registration, a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), courtesy name Shitai, first in seniority, aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month]. His great-grandfather was Shan Yizhong; his grandfather was Shan Shineng; his father is Shan Youde; and his mother is née Wang. Both his parents and grandparents are living. His younger brothers are Shan Shikang and Shan Shizhao. He married née Yang. He placed thirty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yu 李郁 [native of Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, of civilian registration, a Emissary specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji), courtesy name Ruoxu, fifth in seniority, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Li Renjing; his grandfather was Li Jiying; his father is Li Dugong [Vice Magistrate of Lushi County, Henan]; his mother was née Yu; and his stepmother is née Zhou. Both his father and stepmother are living. His elder brother is Li Tong. He married née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Zhong 秦中 [native of Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, of civilian registration, a Prefectural Student specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing), courtesy name Shizhong, second in seniority, aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Qin Yanbin; his grandfather was Qin Cheng; his father is Qin Yunzhe; and his mother is née Li. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Qin Jingyu. He married née Pan. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳瓚〔貫河南開封府陽武縣民籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字重器，行二，年三十二，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖鼎；祖宗；父忠；母孟氏，繼母賈氏。慈侍下。兄榮，弟瑄、琳、瑛。娶李氏。河南鄉試第十三名，會試第六十九名。

李璨〔貫福建福州府福清縣軍籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字子珍，行四，年四十三，十二月三十日生〕。曾祖必美；祖伯紹；父俊；母劉氏。永感下。娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第三十二名，會試第五十七名。

方澥〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字源深，行一，年四十九，十二月二十八日生〕。曾祖作楫；祖環；父努；母吳氏，繼母李氏。具慶下。弟沱、新、洀、汜、洲。娶顧氏，繼娶郭氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第四十六名。

張斌〔貫直隸廣平府永年縣民籍，府學增廣生，治《禮記》，字文質，行一，年二十五，正月十二日生〕。曾祖才〔元任驛丞〕；祖成；父宗顏；母畢氏。具慶下。娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第二十八名，會試第八十名。
translation_en:
Chen Zan 陳瓚, registered in a civilian household of Yangwu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a County Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Zhongqi, he was the second son in his generation, and he was thirty-two sui, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chen Ding, his grandfather was Chen Zong, his father was Chen Zhong, his mother was née Meng, and his stepmother was née Jia. His stepmother was living and his father was deceased. He had an elder brother, Chen Rong, and younger brothers, Chen Xuan, Chen Lin, and Chen Ying, and was married to née Li. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Can 李璨, registered in a military household of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a County Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); his courtesy name was Zizhen, he was the fourth son in his generation, and he was forty-three sui, born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Li Bimei, his grandfather was Li Boshao, his father was Li Jun, and his mother was née Liu. Both his parents were deceased. He was married to née Zheng. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Xie 方澥, registered in a military household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); his courtesy name was Yuanshen, he was the first son in his generation, and he was forty-nine sui, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Fang Zuoji, his grandfather was Fang Huan, his father was Fang Nu, his mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Li. His father and stepmother were both living. He had younger brothers, Fang Tuo, Fang Xin, Fang Pan, Fang Si, and Fang Zhou; he was married to née Gu, and remarried to née Guo. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bin 張斌, registered in a civilian household of Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, was an Added Prefectural Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); his courtesy name was Wenzhi, he was the first son in his generation, and he was twenty-five sui, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhang Cai (who served under the Yuan dynasty as an Assistant Postal Relay Station Master), his grandfather was Zhang Cheng, his father was Zhang Zongyan, and his mother was née Bi. Both his parents were living. He was married to née Guo. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉善慶〔貫江西吉安府萬安縣，民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字祐之，行二，年三十一，四月十四日生〕。曾祖明德〔元任四川知事〕，祖敬先，父彥達〔直隸淮安府學教授〕，母曾氏。具慶下，兄餘慶，娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第四十六名，會試第七十九名。

王銳〔貫直隸永平府遷安縣，民籍，府學生，治《易經》，字允威，行四，年二十七，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖克中，祖可敬，父通〔河南許州判官，致仕〕，嫡母劉氏，母趙氏。具慶下，兄欽、鐸、釗，娶傅氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第八十九名。

焦從周〔貫湖廣郴州興寧縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治《書經》，字孟文，行八，年二十七，四月初八日生〕。曾祖必政，祖慶華〔封吏科給事中〕，父起良〔戶科都給事中〕，母楊氏〔封孺人〕。重慶下，娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第八名，會試第二十二名。

translation_en:
Liu Shanqing 劉善慶 (registered in Wan'an County 萬安縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西, under civilian household status; National University Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing 易經]; courtesy name Youzhi 祐之; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Mingde 明德 (who served as an Administrative Clerk in Sichuan 四川 under the Yuan dynasty), his grandfather was Jingxian 敬先, his father is Yanda 彥達 (Instructor of the Prefectural School of Huai'an Prefecture 淮安府 in the Metropolitan Area [Zhili 直隸]), and his mother is née Zeng 曾氏. Both parents are living; he has an elder brother, Yuqing 餘慶, and is married to née Guo 郭氏. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefectural 順天府 Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rui 王銳 (registered in Qian'an County 遷安縣, Yongping Prefecture 永平府, in the Metropolitan Area [Zhili 直隸], under civilian household status; Prefectural School Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing 易經]; courtesy name Yunwei 允威; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Kezhong 克中, his grandfather was Kejing 可敬, his father is Tong 通 (retired Assistant Prefect of Xuzhou 許州 in Henan 河南), his principal mother is née Liu 劉氏, and his birth mother is née Zhao 趙氏. Both parents are living; he has elder brothers Qin 欽, Duo 鐸, and Zhao 釗, and is married to née Fu 傅氏. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefectural 順天府 Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiao Congzhou 焦從周 (registered in Xingning County 興寧縣, Chenzhou 郴州, Huguang 湖廣, under civilian household status; Added Student of the County School specializing in the Classic of History [Shujing 書經]; courtesy name Mengwen 孟文; eighth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Bizheng 必政, his grandfather is Qinghua 慶華 (invested with the title of Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel), his father is Qiliang 起良 (Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue), and his mother is née Yang 楊氏 (invested as Child-Nurturess). Both grandparents and parents are living; he is married to née Li 李氏. He placed eighth in the Huguang 湖廣 Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Yi 蕭翼 (registered in Yongxin County 永新縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西, under military household status; County School Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing 易經]; courtesy name Tiquan 體全; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Yunke 雲可, his grandfather was Shaozong 紹宗, his father is Kedao 可道, his mother was née Zhang 張氏, and his stepmother is née Zou 鄒氏. His father and stepmother are both living; he has an elder brother, Zhizai 祇載, and a younger brother, Jing 敬, and he was married to née Yan 顏氏 and remarried to née Yuan 袁氏. He placed twenty-third in the Jiangxi 江西 Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Mao 李茂 (registered under a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; a County Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yuemao; third in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month). His great-grandfather was Yu Liang 良 [Palace Attendant Censor in the Yuan dynasty]; his grandfather was Yu Xun 詢 [Prefect of Wenzhou Prefecture 温州府]; his father was Yu Jin 進 [Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan]; and his mother is née Qi 齊. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Yu Rui 瑞 and Yu Ying 瑛 [Magistrate of Xi County 息縣], and his younger brother is Yu Cong 琮. He married a woman née Hu 胡. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi 李時 [registered in a civilian household of Zhending County 真定縣, Zhending Prefecture 真定府, Directly Attached Territory (Zhili); Prefectural School Student; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Xizhi 習之; third in seniority among his brothers; age thirty-four; born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month]. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Chen 謝琛 [registered in a saltern household of Dinghai County 定海縣, Ningbo Prefecture 寧波府, Zhejiang 浙江; County School Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Boyu 伯玉; first in seniority among his brothers; age twenty-eight; born on the second day of the twelfth month]. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ne 王訥 [registered in a civilian household of Wuxi County 無錫縣, Changzhou Prefecture 常州府, Directly Attached Territory (Zhili); Added Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Minxing 敏行; third in seniority among his brothers; age twenty-six; born on the twenty-seventh day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Yanzhi 彥質; his grandfather was Wang Dezhen 德真; his father is Wang Jingshen 景深; his deceased mother was née Qian 錢; and his stepmother is née Gu 顧. His father and stepmother are both living. His elder brothers are Wang Minji 敏吉 and Wang Minli 敏禮, and his younger brother is Wang Minxue 敏學. He married a woman née Qian 錢. Both parents are living; his elder brothers are Liu Jun 濬, Liu Hong 洪, and Liu Yan 演; he is married to Lady Hu 胡氏. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural 順天府 Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ze 王澤 (registered in a military household of Ruzhou Department 汝州, Nanyang Prefecture 南陽府, Henan 河南; Department Student; specialized in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Jimin 濟民; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-three sui, born on the eleventh day of the third month). His mother is living; his elder brother is Wang Zhen 震 and his younger brother is Wang Xuan 選; he is married to Lady Gu 古氏. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Gong 楊貢 (registered in a civilian household of Le'an County 樂安縣, Fuzhou Prefecture 撫州府, Jiangxi 江西; County Student; specialized in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Yankui 彥魁; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-three sui, born on the fifth day of the eleventh month). Both parents are deceased; his elder brother is Yang Yanqi 彥竒; he is married to Lady Zhang 張氏. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Xiang 毛祥 (registered in a civilian household of Xiping County 西平縣, Runing Prefecture 汝寧府, Henan 河南; County Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Yuanji 原吉; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-two sui, born on the second day of the first month). 王彧
貫直隸大名府開州民籍　州學生
治書經字秉文行一年三十四十一月二十九日生
曾祖元善〔元任河中府同知〕祖輔　父勉　母班氏　繼母馬氏
重慶下　弟文　信　僖　儀　伸　娶李氏
順天府鄉試第六名　會試第七十六名
===
李遜
貫江西建昌府南豐縣軍籍　岳州府學生
治詩經字時敏行一年三十五十一月初七日生
曾祖文盛　祖伯儀　父應祖〔國子監助教〕　母曾氏
繼母熊氏　具慶下　弟義生　娶秦氏
湖廣鄉試第七名　會試第九十二名
劉同
貫江西吉安府廬陵縣民籍直隸高陽縣學增廣生
治詩經字伯詢行一年三十四二月初五日生
曾祖樂山　祖嘉會〔武進縣丞〕　父翌之　母陳氏　繼母董氏
重慶下　弟仲坦　叔啓　祖常　宗緒　娶蕭氏
順天府鄉試第二十七名　會試第九十五名
punctuated:
李柰，貫江西廣信府上饒縣，民籍，冠帶舉人，治《易經》，字景春，行七，年三十五，九月十五日生。曾祖逹輕，祖清逺，父彦祥，母陳氏。慈侍下。兄應春、逢春、茂春，弟常春。娶徐氏。江西鄉試第三十八名，會試第七十四名。

王彧，貫直隸大名府開州，民籍，州學生，治《書經》，字秉文，行一，年三十四，十一月二十九日生。曾祖元善〔元任河中府同知〕，祖輔，父勉，母班氏，繼母馬氏。重慶下。弟文、信、僖、儀、伸。娶李氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第七十六名。

李遜，貫江西建昌府南豐縣，軍籍，岳州府學生，治《詩經》，字時敏，行一，年三十五，十一月初七日生。曾祖文盛，祖伯儀，父應祖〔國子監助教〕，母曾氏，繼母熊氏。具慶下。弟義生。娶秦氏。湖廣鄉試第七名，會試第九十二名。

劉同，貫江西吉安府廬陵縣，民籍，直隸高陽縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字伯詢，行一，年二十四，二月初五日生。曾祖樂山，祖嘉會〔武進縣丞〕，父習之，母陳氏，繼母董氏。重慶下。弟仲坦、叔咨、祖常、宗緒。娶蕭氏。順天府鄉試第二十七名，會試第九十五名。
translation_en:
Li Nai 李柰, registered in a commoner household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, is a provincial graduate (juren) granted cap and belt who specializes in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name is Jingchun, he is seventh in seniority among his brothers, and he is thirty-five sui, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Li Daqing, his grandfather was Li Qingyuan, his father was Li Yanxiang, and his mother is née Chen. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Yingchun, Fengchun, and Maochun, and his younger brother is Changchun; he is married to née Xu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yu 王彧, registered in a commoner household in Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, is a subprefectural Confucian school student who specializes in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); his courtesy name is Bingwen, he is first in seniority among his brothers, and he is thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Wang Yuanshan (who served in the Yuan dynasty as Vice Prefect of Hezhong Prefecture), his grandfather is Wang Fu, his father is Wang Mian, his mother was née Ban, and his stepmother is née Ma. Both his grandparents and parents are living. His younger brothers are Wen, Xin, Xi, Yi, and Shen; he is married to née Li. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefectural Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xun 李遜, registered in a military household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, is a student of the Yuezhou Prefectural School who specializes in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); his courtesy name is Shimin, he is first in seniority among his brothers, and he is thirty-five sui, born on the seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Li Wensheng, his grandfather was Li Boyi, his father is Li Yingzu (Instructor in the Directorate of Education), his mother was née Zeng, and his stepmother is née Xiong. Both his father and stepmother are living. His younger brother is Yisheng; he is married to née Qin. He placed seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tong 劉同, registered in a commoner household in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, is an added student (zengguang sheng) of the Gaoyang County School in Zhili who specializes in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); his courtesy name is Boxun, he is first in seniority among his brothers, and he is twenty-four sui, born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Liu Leshan, his grandfather is Liu Jiahui (Assistant Magistrate of Wujin County), his father is Liu Xizhi, his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother is née Dong. Both his grandparents and parents are living. His younger brothers are Zhongtan, Shuzi, Zuchang, and Zongxu; he is married to née Xiao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefectural Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
鄭崇〔貫福建福州府懷安縣民籍，儒士，治《春秋》，字尚德，行六，年五十，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖熒；祖公彥；父振，母徐氏。永感下。兄永。娶楊氏。福建鄉試第一百十二名，會試第七十一名。

成始終〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣民籍，儒士，治《書經》，字敬之，行一，年三十七，九月十八日生〕。曾祖榮七；祖玉山；父彥文，母夏氏。嚴侍下。娶杜氏。應天府鄉試第三十六名，會試第三十八名。

李善〔貫陝西鳳翔府岐山縣軍籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字元吉，行二，年二十九，十一月二十四日生〕。曾祖賢；祖仲祥；父鑑，母王氏。重慶下。兄得喜，弟吉、譽。娶張氏。陝西鄉試第十名，會試第五十四名。

劉益〔貫江西廣信府貴溪縣民籍，縣學生，治《禮記》，字謙之，行十二，年三十五，正月初四日生〕。曾祖汶軒；祖用民；父克淵，母胡氏，繼母彭氏。具慶下。兄濟、澄。娶鄧氏。江西鄉試第五名，會試第三十二名。
translation_en:
Zheng Chong 鄭崇 [registered in a civilian household of Huai'an County 懷安縣, Fuzhou Prefecture 福州府, Fujian 福建; Confucian scholar (rushi); specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Shangde 尚德; sixth in seniority among his brothers; aged fifty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Zheng Ying 鄭熒; his grandfather was Zheng Gongyan 鄭公彥; his father was Zheng Zhen 鄭振, and his mother was née Xu 徐氏. Both his parents are deceased (yonggan xia). His elder brother is Zheng Yong 鄭永. He married née Yang 楊氏. He placed 112th in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 71st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shizhong 成始終 [registered in a civilian household of Wuxi County 無錫縣, Changzhou Prefecture 常州府, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸); Confucian scholar (rushi); specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Jingzhi 敬之; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Cheng Rongqi 成榮七; his grandfather was Cheng Yushan 成玉山; his father is Cheng Yanwen 成彥文, and his mother was née Xia 夏氏. His father is living and his mother is deceased (yanshi xia). He married née Du 杜氏. He placed 36th in the Yingtian Prefecture 應天府 Provincial Examination and 38th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shan 李善 [registered in a military household of Qishan County 岐山縣, Fengxiang Prefecture 鳳翔府, Shaanxi 陝西; County School Student (xian xuesheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Yuanji 元吉; second in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month]. His great-grandfather was Li Xian 李賢; his grandfather is Li Zhongxiang 李仲祥; his father is Li Jian 李鑑, and his mother is née Wang 王氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living (chongqing xia). His elder brother is Li Dexi 李得喜, and his younger brothers are Li Ji 李吉 and Li Yu 李譽. He married née Zhang 張氏. He placed 10th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 54th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yi 劉益 [registered in a civilian household of Guixi County 貴溪縣, Guangxin Prefecture 廣信府, Jiangxi 江西; County School Student (xian xuesheng); specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Qianzhi 謙之; twelfth in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Liu Wenxuan 劉汶軒; his grandfather was Liu Yongmin 劉用民; his father is Liu Keyuan 劉克淵, his mother was née Hu 胡氏, and his stepmother is née Peng 彭氏. Both his father and stepmother are living (juqing xia). His elder brothers are Liu Ji 劉濟 and Liu Cheng 劉澄. He married née Deng 鄧氏. He placed 5th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 32nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉訓〔貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣民籍，縣學生，治《春秋》，字忠言，行三，年三十六，七月二十八日生〕。曾祖貴卿；祖夢〔封監察御史〕；父從憲；母桂氏。慈侍下。兄謙、讓；弟諲。娶喻氏。湖廣鄉試第四名，會試第六十二名。

劉觀〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣軍籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字崇觀，行三，年三十二，七月初四日生〕。曾祖道彰；祖子同；父宗平〔翰林院檢討〕；母解氏。慈侍下。兄晉、益〔兵科給事中〕。娶黃氏，繼娶李氏。江西鄉試第一名，會試第五十八名。

郭仲南〔貫浙江金華府蘭谿縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《易經》，字仲南，行二，年三十四，六月二十六日生〕。曾祖文中；祖明德；父叔榮；母方氏。具慶下。兄仲宣；弟昊、冕；從弟仲曦〔都察院照磨〕。娶周氏。浙江鄉試第三十九名，會試第二十四名。

尚褫〔貫河南汝寧府羅山縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《春秋》，字景福，行二，年三十一，五月十九日生〕。曾祖仲賢〔元萬戶〕；祖伯通〔元萬戶〕；父志；母張氏。具慶下。兄虒；從兄本〔滄州判官〕；弟琥。娶戴氏。河南鄉試第四名，會試第八十三名。
translation_en:
Liu Xun 劉訓 (native of Macheng County 麻城縣, Huangzhou Prefecture 黃州府, Huguang 湖廣, of civilian registration; County School Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Zhongyan 忠言; third in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Liu Guiqing 貴卿; his grandfather was Liu Meng 夢 (invested with the title of Investigating Censor); his father was Liu Congxian 從憲; and his mother is née Gui 桂氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Liu Qian 謙 and Liu Rang 讓, and his younger brother is Liu Yin 諲. He married née Yu 喻氏. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Guan 劉觀 (native of Jishui County 吉水縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西, of military registration; County School Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Chongguan 崇觀; third in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Liu Daozhang 道彰; his grandfather was Liu Zitong 子同; his father was Liu Zongping 宗平 (Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy); and his mother is née Xie 解氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Liu Jin 晉 and Liu Yi 益 (Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War). He married née Huang 黃氏, and took née Li 李氏 as his second wife. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zhongnan 郭仲南 (native of Lanxi County 蘭谿縣, Jinhua Prefecture 金華府, Zhejiang 浙江, of civilian registration; Added Student of the County School specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zhongnan 仲南; second in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Guo Wenzhong 文中; his grandfather was Guo Mingde 明德; his father is Guo Shurong 叔榮; and his mother is née Fang 方氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Guo Zhongxuan 仲宣; his younger brothers are Guo Hao 昊 and Guo Mian 冕; and his younger paternal cousin is Guo Zhongxi 仲曦 (Record Keeper in the Censorate). He married née Zhou 周氏. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Chi 尚褫 (native of Luoshan County 羅山縣, Runing Prefecture 汝寧府, Henan 河南, of civilian registration; Added Student of the County School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Jingfu 景福; second in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-one, born on the nineteenth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Shang Zhongxian 仲賢 (Brigade Commander in the Yuan dynasty); his grandfather was Shang Botong 伯通 (Brigade Commander in the Yuan dynasty); his father is Shang Zhi 志; and his mother is née Zhang 張氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Shang Si 虒; his elder paternal cousin is Shang Ben 本 (Assistant Prefect of Cangzhou 滄州); and his younger brother is Shang Hu 琥. He married née Dai 戴氏. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:

His elder brothers are Lin 林, [?], and [?], his younger brother is Sen 森, and he is married to née Liu 劉氏. translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: "The Way of the Emperors and Kings is fully recorded in the Classics. Confucius compiled and completed them, beginning from Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and extending down to the Zhou, making them a model and standard for ten thousand generations, all of which can be taken up and put into practice. Coming down to the Han, the Tang, and thereafter, worthy and wise rulers looked up with admiration to these fine plans and faithfully followed the constant norms in seeking good order and tranquility, and all of them accomplished things worthy of praise and record. At those times, the worthy men and noble gentlemen who came forth to accept employment in the world likewise without exception offered their loyalty and contributed their counsel in order to assist…

Yet when one examines their accomplishments in bringing about order, compared with what is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of History (Shu), they fall short. Why is this [reading 他 as 也]? Reflecting deeply upon Our dynasty, the successive Sacred Emperors have followed one after another, earnestly revering the ancient Way so as to exalt supreme governance—how lofty and majestic is its flourishing! Now We have succeeded to the great hereditary mandate and truly cherish the duty of carrying forward and recounting their work, allowing Ourselves no leisure from dawn to night, hoping that together with Our officials and people We may all ascend to a state of contented harmony. translation_en:
… and the sequence of putting it into practice must have its proper fitness. You gentlemen have been promoted and advanced through your illumination of the Classics; as for the methods of bringing your ruler to perfection and bestowing blessings upon the people, you have studied them thoroughly beforehand and must possess substantive insights. Set them forth clearly in your essays, neither speaking in empty generalities nor holding anything back, for We shall personally review them.

The second day of the third month of the fourth year of the Zhengtong era (March 17, 1439).

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
臣施槃
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於德帝王之德本乎敬
非德不足以為治非敬不足以成德善治天下
者未有不本乎德善修德者未有不本乎敬堯
舜之所以公天下而躋世雍熈者此敬也禹湯
文武之所以家天下而措世隆平者此敬也漢
唐宋之君所以不可與二帝三王齒而治不古
若者庸非此心之敬德有替乎易曰明出地上
晉君子以自昭明德孔子曰為政以德然非敬
則德無以成故又曰敬以直內修己以敬焉欽
===
惟
皇帝陛下以聰明睿智之資備剛健中正之德曩在
青宮仁孝之聲已播聞于中外及夫
嗣登大寶不殖貨利不事遊畋無稽之言勿聽弗
詢之謀勿庸日
御經帷講求
聖學臣有以知
皇上誠大有為之君太平之治固已至矣而
皇上之心不自足焉乃進臣等于
廷降賜

punctuated:
臣施槃。

臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於德，帝王之德本乎敬。非德不足以為治，非敬不足以成德。善治天下者，未有不本乎德；善修德者，未有不本乎敬。堯、舜之所以公天下而躋世雍熈者，此敬也；禹、湯、文、武之所以家天下而措世隆平者，此敬也；漢、唐、宋之君所以不可與二帝、三王齒，而治不古若者，庸非此心之敬德有替乎？《易》曰：「明出地上，晉；君子以自昭明德。」孔子曰：「為政以德。」然非敬則德無以成，故又曰：「敬以直內。」「修己以敬」焉。

欽惟皇帝陛下，以聰明睿智之資，備剛健中正之德。曩在青宮，仁孝之聲已播聞于中外。及夫嗣登大寶，不殖貨利，不事遊畋，無稽之言勿聽，弗詢之謀勿庸，日御經帷，講求聖學，臣有以知皇上誠大有為之君，太平之治固已至矣。而皇上之心不自足焉，乃進臣等于廷，降賜
translation_en:
Your servant Shi Pan 施槃.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in virtue, and the virtue of emperors and kings is rooted in reverence. Without virtue, one cannot achieve good governance; without reverence, one cannot bring virtue to completion. Among those skilled at governing All-under-Heaven, there has never been one who did not take virtue as his root; among those skilled at cultivating virtue, there has never been one who did not take reverence as his root. That whereby Yao 堯 and Shun 舜 treated All-under-Heaven as a public trust and raised the world to harmonious prosperity was this reverence; that whereby Yu 禹, Tang 湯, King Wen 文, and King Wu 武 made All-under-Heaven a family heritage and placed the world in flourishing peace was this reverence. As for why the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song could not be ranked alongside the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and why their governance did not match that of antiquity—was it not because the reverent virtue of this mind suffered decline? The Book of Changes (Yi 易) says: "Brightness rises above the earth: Advance (Jin 晉). Thus the noble man himself brightens his bright virtue." Confucius said: "Exercise governance by means of virtue." Yet without reverence, there is no way for virtue to be brought to completion; therefore it is also said, "Reverence to straighten the inner life," and "He cultivates himself with reverence."

With reverence I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty, endowed with keen intelligence and sage wisdom, possesses the virtues of firm strength and central uprightness. Formerly, when in the Eastern Palace as Heir Apparent, the reputation of Your benevolence and filial piety had already spread throughout the court and the provinces. And when You succeeded to and ascended the Great Treasure, You did not amass wealth and profit, nor indulge in excursions and hunting; unsubstantiated words You did not heed, and counsels not deliberated upon You did not employ. Daily You attend the Classic Colloquium (jingwei 經帷) to study and pursue the learning of the sages. By this, Your servant knows that Your Majesty is truly a ruler capable of great achievements, and that the governance of Great Peace has assuredly already arrived. Yet Your Majesty's mind is not self-satisfied; You have therefore summoned Your servants to the court and graciously bestowed…

text:
清問首稽帝王德見於治之實次考漢唐宋治不
逮古之由終之以
今日謹始圖成之要推行後先之序且以夙夜匪
遑為言者臣又有以知
皇上是心即望道未見之心誠國家生民之福謹拜
手稽首為天下賀𥡴
皇上永懷是心而不忘也請因
聖問所及而陳之臣聞天生斯民而必樹之君聖人
君天下而必本之德聖人之德無他焉敬而已
矣稽諸古帝堯之欽明文思克明俊德而黎民
===
有於變之休舜之温恭允塞由仁義行而四方
有風動之效此二帝之以敬為德而成治也禹
之祗承于帝克勤克儉而文命敷于四海湯之
聖敬日躋克寬克仁而彰信兆民穆穆文王緝
熙敬止是以純亦不已而萬民咸和執競武王
無競維烈是以丕單稱德而萬姓悅服此三王
之以敬修德而致治也二帝三王敬以存心出
治之道著於易寓於書詠歌於詩孔子有是敬
有是德而無其位從而刪定係作纂而成之肇
自唐虞訖于周以為千載之準繩萬世之楷範

有於變之休舜之溫恭允塞由仁義行而四方
有風動之效此二帝之以敬為德而成治也禹
之祗承于帝克勤克儉而文命敷于四海湯之

punctuated:
清問，首稽帝王德見於治之實，次考漢、唐、宋治不逮古之由，終之以今日謹始圖成之要、推行後先之序，且以「夙夜匪遑」為言者。臣又有以知皇上是心，即望道未見之心，誠國家生民之福。謹拜手稽首，為天下賀，𥡴皇上永懷是心而不忘也。請因聖問所及而陳之。
臣聞天生斯民，而必樹之君；聖人君天下，而必本之德。聖人之德無他焉，敬而已矣。稽諸古，帝堯之欽明文思，克明俊德，而黎民有於變之休；舜之温恭允塞，由仁義行，而四方有風動之效。此二帝之以敬為德而成治也。禹之祗承于帝，克勤克儉，而文命敷于四海；湯之聖敬日躋，克寬克仁，而彰信兆民；穆穆文王，緝熙敬止，是以純亦不已，而萬民咸和；執競武王，無競維烈，是以丕單稱德，而萬姓悅服。此三王之以敬修德而致治也。二帝三王敬以存心，出治之道，著於《易》，寓於《書》，詠歌於《詩》。孔子有是敬、有是德而無其位，從而刪定、係作、纂而成之，肇自唐、虞，訖于周，以為千載之準繩、萬世之楷範，
translation_en:
… pure inquiry, first examining the reality of how the Emperors and Kings manifested their virtue in governance, next investigating the reasons why the governance of the Han, Tang, and Song failed to reach that of antiquity, and concluding with the essentials of being cautious at the beginning and planning for completion today, the sequence of priorities in carrying them out, and furthermore speaking of "not having leisure from morning to night." From this your servant also knows that this mind of Your Majesty is indeed the mind that looks toward the Way as though not yet seeing it—truly a blessing for the state and the people! I謹 [humbly] bow my hands to the ground and knock my head to congratulate All Under Heaven, and pray that Your Majesty will forever cherish this mind and never forget it. Allow me to set forth my views based on what Your Sacred Inquiry has touched upon.

Your servant has heard that when Heaven gives birth to these people, It necessarily establishes a ruler for them; when a sage rules All Under Heaven, he necessarily takes virtue as his foundation. The virtue of the sage is nothing other than reverence alone. Examining antiquity, Emperor Yao was reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful; he was able to make illustrious his lofty virtue, and the black-haired people enjoyed the blessing of universal transformation. Shun was mild, respectful, sincerely upright; he acted out of benevolence and righteousness, and the four quarters experienced the effect of being moved as by the wind. This was how the Two Emperors took reverence as their virtue and accomplished good governance. Yu reverently received from the Sovereign, was able to be diligent and frugal, and his civilizing ordinances were spread throughout the four seas. Tang's sagely reverence daily ascended; he was able to be宽 [magnanimous] and benevolent, and manifested trustworthiness to the millions of people. Profound and solemn was King Wen, continuously bright in his reverent resting place; therefore his purity was unceasing, and the myriad people were all harmonious. Holding fast to strength was King Wu, matchless in his功烈 [meritorious achievements]; therefore he greatly and wholly matched his virtue, and the myriad surnames gladly submitted. This was how the Three Kings cultivated virtue through reverence and brought about good governance. The Two Emperors and Three Kings preserved their minds with reverence, and the Way by which they brought forth governance is made manifest in the Book of Changes (Yi), lodged in the Book of Documents (Shu), and chanted in the Book of Odes (Shi). Confucius possessed this reverence and possessed this virtue, yet lacked the position of a ruler; accordingly, he excised and fixed, appended and composed, compiling and completing them, beginning from Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] down to the Zhou, to serve as a standard for a thousand years and a model for ten thousand generations, …

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
誠可舉而行可遵而守也歷周而下言治者曰
漢唐宋在漢則高帝以馬上得天下不事詩書
而終雜於伯道文帝則禮樂教化謙讓未遑而
不純於王德二君者天資寛厚雖有可稱然皆
未至於帝王之治臣不欲為
皇上陳之也繼之者武帝之罷黜百家表章六經善
矣然天資多慾窮奢極侈而海內虛耗明帝尊
師重傅臨雍拜老似矣然天資苛薄器度未宏
而吏事深刻况當時輔治之臣若蕭何之啓侈
陳平之任智公孫之飾詐桓榮之章句其去唐
===
虞三代之佐蓋遠矣此漢之所以止於漢也在
唐則太宗求賢納諫崇儒講學拳拳於周禮一
書固有志於三代之治矣然大綱未正而不免
雜胡夷之風在宋則仁宗修明禮樂仁厚風行
昔人謂法堯舜惟法仁宗信矣然眾目未舉而
不過為因循之政况當時輔治之臣房杜之徒
無能於禮樂呂王之儔未純乎道義其視唐虞
三代之佐有間矣此唐宋之所以止於唐宋也
是則漢唐宋之所以不能上繼唐虞三代而稱
善治者政以為之君者不能以敬修德而為出

punctuated: 誠可舉而行，可遵而守也。歷周而下，言治者曰漢、唐、宋。在漢，則高帝以馬上得天下，不事《詩》、《書》，而終雜於伯道；文帝則禮樂教化，謙讓未遑，而不純於王德。二君者，天資寛厚，雖有可稱，然皆未至於帝王之治，臣不欲為皇上陳之也。繼之者，武帝之罷黜百家，表章《六經》，善矣；然天資多慾，窮奢極侈，而海內虛耗。明帝尊師重傅，臨雍拜老，似矣；然天資苛薄，器度未宏，而吏事深刻。况當時輔治之臣，若蕭何之啓侈、陳平之任智、公孫之飾詐、桓榮之章句，其去唐、虞、三代之佐，蓋遠矣。此漢之所以止於漢也。在唐，則太宗求賢納諫，崇儒講學，拳拳於《周禮》一書，固有志於三代之治矣；然大綱未正，而不免雜胡夷之風。在宋，則仁宗修明禮樂，仁厚風行，昔人謂「法堯、舜，惟法仁宗」，信矣；然眾目未舉，而不過為因循之政。况當時輔治之臣，房、杜之徒，無能於禮樂；呂、王之儔，未純乎道義。其視唐、虞、三代之佐，有間矣。此唐、宋之所以止於唐、宋也。是則漢、唐、宋之所以不能上繼唐、虞、三代而稱善治者，政以為之君者，不能以敬修德而為出
translation_en: …—truly they can be taken up and put into practice, followed and preserved. Passing down from the Zhou, those who speak of good governance name the Han, Tang, and Song. In the Han, Emperor Gao won the empire on horseback, did not occupy himself with the Book of Odes (Shi) and Book of Documents (Shu), and in the end mixed his rule with the way of the hegemon; Emperor Wen, for his part, modestly declined to find the leisure for rites, music, and moral transformation, and so was not pure in kingly virtue. Although the generous and magnanimous natural endowments of these two rulers are worthy of praise, neither attained the governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings, and your servant does not wish to set them forth before Your Majesty. Among those who succeeded them, Emperor Wu's dismissal of the Hundred Schools and elevation of the Six Classics was good indeed; yet by nature he had many desires, indulged in extreme luxury and extravagance, and left the realm within the seas depleted and exhausted. Emperor Ming's honoring of teachers and valuing of tutors, and his visiting the Imperial University (Biyong) to bow before the aged, seemed the part; yet by nature he was harsh and ungenerous, his capacity was not broad, and his administrative affairs were severe and exacting. Moreover, as for the ministers who assisted in governance at the time—such as Xiao He 蕭何 with his encouragement of extravagance, Chen Ping 陳平 with his reliance on clever stratagems, Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 with his disguised deceit, and Huan Rong 桓榮 with his mere chapter-and-verse scholarship—they were far removed indeed from the aides of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. This is why the Han remained merely the Han. In the Tang, Emperor Taizong sought out the worthy and accepted remonstrance, revered Confucianism and lectured on learning, and held fast to the single book of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), truly possessing the ambition for the governance of the Three Dynasties; yet the great fundamental principles were not rectified, and his rule could not avoid being mixed with barbarian customs. In the Song, Emperor Renzong cultivated and clarified rites and music, and benevolence and generosity prevailed as the custom; when men of the past said, "To model oneself on Yao and Shun, one need only model oneself on Renzong," it was true indeed; yet the myriad specific details of governance were not raised up, and it amounted to no more than a politics of routine complacency. Moreover, as for the ministers who assisted in governance at those times, men like Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 and Du Ruhui 杜如晦 were incapable in rites and music, while peers such as Lü Yijian 呂夷簡 and Wang Zeng 王曾 [?] were not pure in the Way and its righteousness. Compared with the aides of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, there was a gap between them. This is why the Tang and Song remained merely the Tang and Song. Thus, the reason why the Han, Tang, and Song were unable to succeed upwardly to Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties and be acclaimed for ideal governance is precisely that those who served as their rulers were unable to cultivate virtue through reverence as the basis for issuing…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
治之本為之臣者不能以敬格君而盡輔治之
要雖皆景仰適遵以圖至治而卒無其實雖欲
獻忠效謀以匡乃辟而未底其極臣不欲以是
望於
盛世之
君臣也伏惟
天朝
列聖相承敦崇古道以隆至治巍巍乎其至盛誠如
皇上之言矣
皇上嗣大歷服允懷継述夙夜匪遑
===
聖心之敬與帝王敬以存心同一機期與臣民咸躋
熈皞則
聖世之治必與帝王德以致治同一致然猶
詢臣以謹始圖成謂必有其要推行之序謂必有
其宜臣愚不足以知此然嘗聞商書有之曰慎
厥終惟其始欽崇天道永保天命又曰弗慮胡
獲弗為胡成一人元良萬邦以貞此則慎始圖
終之要也然約而言之不外乎一敬而已孔子
言九經之序曰修身也尊賢也親親也敬大臣
也體群臣也子庶民也来百工也柔遠人也懷

punctuated: 治之本，為之臣者不能以敬格君而盡輔治之要。雖皆景仰適遵以圖至治，而卒無其實；雖欲獻忠效謀以匡乃辟，而未底其極。臣不欲以是望於盛世之君臣也。伏惟天朝列聖相承，敦崇古道，以隆至治，巍巍乎其至盛，誠如皇上之言矣。皇上嗣大歷服，允懷継述，夙夜匪遑，聖心之敬與帝王敬以存心同一機；期與臣民咸躋熈皞，則聖世之治必與帝王德以致治同一致。然猶詢臣以謹始圖成，謂必有其要；推行之序，謂必有其宜。臣愚不足以知此，然嘗聞《商書》有之曰：「慎厥終，惟其始。欽崇天道，永保天命。」又曰：「弗慮胡獲？弗為胡成？一人元良，萬邦以貞。」此則慎始圖終之要也，然約而言之，不外乎一敬而已。孔子言九經之序曰：「修身也，尊賢也，親親也，敬大臣也，體群臣也，子庶民也，来百工也，柔遠人也，懷
translation_en:
… as the foundation for bringing forth good governance, and those who served as ministers could not rectify their rulers through reverence so as to fulfill the essentials of assisting in governance. Although they all looked up to and followed [the ancients] in hopes of achieving supreme governance, in the end they lacked the reality of it; although they wished to offer loyalty and contribute counsel to rectify their sovereigns, they never reached the ultimate standard. Your servant does not wish to expect only this of the ruler and ministers of this flourishing age.

Humbly, I reflect that the successive sacred emperors of our Celestial Dynasty have inherited the throne one after another, earnestly esteeming the ancient Way so as to exalt supreme governance—how lofty and supremely flourishing it is, truly just as Your Majesty has stated! Your Majesty has succeeded to the great hereditary mandate, sincerely cherishing the continuation and carrying forward of Your predecessors' work, never resting from dawn to night. The reverence of Your Sacred Mind is of the very same vital spring as the ancient emperors and kings preserving their minds through reverence; and since You aspire to ascend together with Your ministers and people to a state of harmonious and vast peace, the governance of this sacred age will surely be of the very same perfection as the ancient emperors and kings achieving good governance through virtue.

Yet You still question Your servant regarding being careful at the beginning and planning for completion, saying there must be an essential principle to it, and regarding the sequence of putting it into practice, saying there must be what is appropriate to it. Your servant is foolish and inadequate to know this, yet I have heard that in the Documents of Shang (Shangshu) it is said: "To be careful of the end, look to the beginning. Reverently honor the Way of Heaven, and forever preserve the Mandate of Heaven." And again it is said: "Without thought, how can anything be gained? Without action, how can anything be completed? When the One Man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby rectified." This, then, is the essential principle of being careful at the beginning and planning for the end; yet to sum it up in a word, it is nothing other than reverence alone. Confucius, in speaking of the sequence of the Nine Standard Rules, said: "Cultivating the person, honoring the worthy, being affectionate to relatives, respecting great ministers, showing体 [sympathetic consideration] to the whole body of officers, treating the common people as one's children, encouraging the hundred artisans to come, showing tenderness to men from afar, and cherishing…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
諸侯也論大學之條目有曰身修而后家齊家
齊而后國治國治而后天下平此則推行先後
之序也然約而言之亦不越乎一敬而已夫敬
者一心之主宰萬事之本根千聖相傳之心法
帝學成始成終之要道堯之允恭舜之恭巳禹
之祗承湯之懋敬文王之懿恭武王之執競此
敬也易之乾乾書之精一詩之思無邪春秋之
謹嚴禮之毋不敬此敬也
皇上誠能存此心之敬而蘊之為德以此德而達之
于治紀綱文章以此敬德而著政教號令本此
===
敬德而推殆見治隆俗美內平外成三辰迭運
而不失其宜四時順行而不拂其序山川鬼神
莫不以寧鳥獸魚鱉罔不咸若可以為堯舜可
以參天地賛化育而保天下之事備矣継志述
事之道盡矣周書有之曰王敬作所不可不敬
德程子曰涵養須用敬此之謂也臣學不足以
致
君澤民謹竭愚陋以獻惟
皇上采擇焉則不勝幸甚臣謹對

punctuated: 諸侯也。」論《大學》之條目有曰：「身修而后家齊，家齊而后國治，國治而后天下平。」此則推行先後之序也。然約而言之，亦不越乎一敬而已。夫敬者，一心之主宰，萬事之本根，千聖相傳之心法，帝學成始成終之要道。堯之「允恭」，舜之「恭巳」，禹之「祗承」，湯之「懋敬」，文王之「懿恭」，武王之「執競」，此敬也；《易》之「乾乾」，《書》之「精一」，《詩》之「思無邪」，《春秋》之「謹嚴」，《禮》之「毋不敬」，此敬也。皇上誠能存此心之敬而蘊之為德，以此德而達之于治，紀綱文章以此敬德而著，政教號令本此敬德而推，殆見治隆俗美，內平外成，三辰迭運而不失其宜，四時順行而不拂其序，山川鬼神莫不以寧，鳥獸魚鱉罔不咸若，可以為堯、舜，可以參天地、賛化育，而保天下之事備矣，継志述事之道盡矣。《周書》有之曰：「王敬作所，不可不敬德。」程子曰：「涵養須用敬。」此之謂也。臣學不足以致君澤民，謹竭愚陋以獻，惟皇上采擇焉，則不勝幸甚。臣謹對。
translation_en:
… the feudal lords." And in discussing the steps of the Great Learning (Daxue), it is said: "When the person is cultivated, then the family is regulated; when the family is regulated, then the state is rightly governed; when the state is rightly governed, then the world is made tranquil." This is the sequence of priority in putting things into practice. Yet to sum it up briefly, this too does not go beyond that single word: reverence.

Now reverence is the master of the single mind, the root of the myriad affairs, the mental discipline handed down through a thousand sages, and the essential Way by which imperial learning brings things from beginning to completion. Yao's "sincere courtesy," Shun's "reverent self-restraint," Yu's "reverent acceptance," Tang's "strenuous reverence," King Wen's "admirable courtesy," and King Wu's "steadfast vigor"—all these are reverence. The "unceasing diligence" of the Book of Changes (Yi), the "refinement and singleness" of the Book of Documents (Shu), the "having no depraved thoughts" of the Book of Odes (Shi), the "strictness and rigor" of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and the "never being without reverence" of the Book of Rites (Li)—all these are reverence.

If Your Majesty can truly preserve the reverence of this mind and accumulate it as virtue, and through this virtue extend it to governance—so that the fundamental laws and cultural institutions are made manifest through this reverent virtue, and governance, education, and commands are extended on the basis of this reverent virtue—then we shall surely see governance flourish and customs become beautiful, the interior pacified and the exterior brought to order, the three luminaries revolving in alternation without losing their proper course, the four seasons proceeding smoothly without violating their sequence, mountains, rivers, and spiritual beings all enjoying tranquility, and birds, beasts, fishes, and turtles all following their natures. Thus Your Majesty may become a Yao or a Shun, may form a triad with Heaven and Earth and assist in the transforming and nourishing processes of nature; the task of preserving the world will be complete, and the Way of carrying forward the intentions and continuing the undertakings of your predecessors will be fulfilled to the utmost.

The Documents of Zhou (Zhoushu) has it: "Let the king make reverence his dwelling-place; he must not fail to revere virtue." Master Cheng (Chengzi) said: "Nurturing the mind requires the use of reverence." This is what is meant.

Your servant's learning is insufficient to bring his sovereign to perfection or to benefit the people, yet he respectfully exhausts his foolish and rustic thoughts to offer them up. If only Your Majesty will select and adopt from them, it will be a blessing beyond measure. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
臣楊鼎
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心
盖心者妙是道之體用實致治之本原也苟存
其心則道由是而出治可得而善矣不存其心
則道由是而昧雖欲善治其可得乎稽諸往古
堯之欽明文思舜之溫恭允塞此二帝之所以
神明其心以妙夫道也禹之惟精惟一湯之以
禮制心文王之小心翼翼武王之無貳爾心此
三王之所以持其心以求夫道也故曰二帝三
王存此心者也欽惟
===
皇帝陛下禀聰明睿智之資備剛健中正之德纘承
列聖之洪圖尊居九五之大位遠宗帝王之道近守
祖宗之法道已至矣望之猶若未至民已安矣視之
猶若未安乃於萬幾之暇又進臣等於
廷賜以
清問首舉帝王為治之道繼以謹始圖成之要推
行之序此皆
陛下之所素知而素行者也豈待愚臣之言哉雖然
臣有以知
陛下之心即古昔聖人不自滿足之心好問好察之

punctuated:
臣楊鼎。
臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。盖心者，妙是道之體用，實致治之本原也。苟存其心，則道由是而出，治可得而善矣；不存其心，則道由是而昧，雖欲善治，其可得乎？稽諸往古，堯之欽明文思，舜之溫恭允塞，此二帝之所以神明其心以妙夫道也；禹之惟精惟一，湯之以禮制心，文王之小心翼翼，武王之無貳爾心，此三王之所以持其心以求夫道也。故曰：「二帝、三王，存此心者也。」欽惟皇帝陛下禀聰明睿智之資，備剛健中正之德，纘承列聖之洪圖，尊居九五之大位，遠宗帝王之道，近守祖宗之法，道已至矣，望之猶若未至；民已安矣，視之猶若未安。乃於萬幾之暇，又進臣等於廷，賜以清問，首舉帝王為治之道，繼以謹始圖成之要、推行之序。此皆陛下之所素知而素行者也，豈待愚臣之言哉？雖然，臣有以知陛下之心，即古昔聖人不自滿足之心、好問好察之
translation_en:
Your servant Yang Ding 楊鼎.
Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of the Five Emperors and Three Kings was rooted in the Way, and the Way of the Emperors and Kings was rooted in the mind. For the mind brings to subtle perfection both the substance and the function of this Way, and is truly the fundamental source of achieving good order. If one preserves one's mind, the Way issues forth from it, and governance can be made good; if one does not preserve one's mind, the Way is thereby obscured, and though one might wish for good governance, how could it be attained? Examining antiquity, the reverence, clarity, cultural accomplishment, and thoughtfulness of Yao 堯, and the warmth, respectfulness, and sincere trustworthiness of Shun 舜—these were how the Two Emperors made their minds spiritually luminous so as to bring the Way to subtle perfection. The pureness and singleness of mind of Yu 禹, the regulating of the mind through ritual propriety of Tang 湯, the cautious and reverent care of King Wen 文王, and the "have no doubleness in your hearts" of King Wu 武王—these were how the Three Kings maintained their minds in order to seek the Way. Therefore it is said: "The Two Emperors and Three Kings were those who preserved this mind."

Reverently I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty is endowed with intelligent, perspicacious, and wise gifts, possesses firm, vigorous, balanced, and upright virtue, has succeeded to the vast design of the line of imperial sages, and occupies in尊 majesty the great throne of the nine-five position. Distantly taking as models the Way of the Emperors and Kings, and closely adhering to the institutions of the Imperial Ancestors, Your Way has already reached perfection, yet You look toward it as though you had not yet reached it; the people are already at peace, yet You regard them as though they were not yet at peace. Thus, in your leisure from the myriad affairs of state, You have summoned your servants to the court and favored us with Your sagely inquiries, first raising the Way by which the Emperors and Kings governed, and following with the essentials of being careful at the beginning and planning for completion, as well as the sequence for putting them into practice. These are all matters that Your Majesty has long known and long practiced—how could they await the words of your foolish servant? Even so, your servant has the means to know that Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind of the sages of antiquity, who were never self-satisfied and who delighted in questioning and examining…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
意也臣雖淺陋欽承
清問敢不拜手稽首以對揚
聖天子之明命乎臣切惟經者聖人載道之器二帝
三王為治之道具載於其間孔子以天縱之聖
任斯道之重當周轍既東之日而不得君師之
位於是退於洙泗之間刪詩書定禮樂讚周易
脩春秋纂集而成六經以為萬世楷範後世人
主有志於二帝三王之道皆可舉而行之若夫
漢承秦而有天下享國四百年中間賢智之君
若武帝之雄才大畧舉用賢能罷黜百家表章
===
六經光武之講論經理勤勞不怠首訪儒雅興
起學校當時若董仲舒之儒術鄧禹之勳業皆
有可稱焉唐繼隋而有天下享國三百年中間
賢智之君若太宗之力行仁義身致太平憲宗
憤積世之弊憫唐室之替善用忠謀不惑群議
當時若房玄齡杜如晦之善謀善斷若李絳之
清直皆有可取焉至於宋有天下若太祖太宗
真宗之為君皆嚮慕隆古時則有若趙普之沉
毅呂蒙正李沆之剛正亦皆足以有為焉君臣
之相遇如此而其致治成功宜可追乎二帝三

意也。臣雖淺陋，欽承清問，敢不拜手稽首，以對揚聖天子之明命乎！

臣切惟經者，聖人載道之器，二帝、三王為治之道具載於其間。孔子以天縱之聖，任斯道之重，當周轍既東之日，而不得君師之位，於是退於洙、泗之間，刪《詩》、《書》，定《禮》、《樂》，讚《周易》，脩《春秋》，纂集而成六經，以為萬世楷範。後世人主有志於二帝、三王之道，皆可舉而行之。

若夫漢承秦而有天下，享國四百年。中間賢智之君，若武帝之雄才大畧，舉用賢能，罷黜百家，表章六經；光武之講論經理，勤勞不怠，首訪儒雅，興起學校；當時若董仲舒之儒術、鄧禹之勳業，皆有可稱焉。唐繼隋而有天下，享國三百年。中間賢智之君，若太宗之力行仁義，身致太平；憲宗憤積世之弊，憫唐室之替，善用忠謀，不惑群議；當時若房玄齡、杜如晦之善謀善斷，若李絳之清直，皆有可取焉。至於宋有天下，若太祖、太宗、真宗之為君，皆嚮慕隆古；時則有若趙普之沉毅，呂蒙正、李沆之剛正，亦皆足以有為焉。君臣之相遇如此，而其致治成功，宜可追乎二帝、三
translation_en:
…intent [to love questioning and examining]. Though your servant is shallow and crude, having reverently received Your pure inquiry, how dare I not bow with hands clasped and head to the ground to respond to and extol the brilliant charge of the Sacred Son of Heaven!

Your servant humbly reflects that the Classics are the vessels in which the sages conveyed the Way, and the Way by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings governed is fully recorded within them. Confucius, with his Heaven-endowed sageliness, took upon himself the heavy burden of this Way. Living in the days after the Zhou royal carriage had moved east, and unable to attain the position of ruler and teacher, he retired to the region between the Zhu 洙 and Si 泗 rivers, where he pared down the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), fixed the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), wrote commentaries on the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi), and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), collecting and editing them to form the Six Classics as a model for ten thousand generations. Any ruler of later ages who sets his mind on the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings can take them up and put them into practice.

As for the Han, it succeeded the Qin in possessing the realm and enjoyed the state for four hundred years. Among the worthy and wise rulers during that time, there were Emperor Wu (Han Wudi 漢武帝), with his heroic talent and grand strategy, who promoted and employed the worthy and capable, dismissed the Hundred Schools, and exalted the Six Classics; and Emperor Guangwu (Han Guangwudi 漢光武帝), who discussed the principles of the Classics, toiled tirelessly, first sought out men of Confucian refinement, and raised up schools. At those times, the Confucian learning of men like Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 and the meritorious achievements of men like Deng Yu 鄧禹 were all worthy of praise. The Tang succeeded the Sui in possessing the realm and enjoyed the state for three hundred years. Among the worthy and wise rulers during that time, there were Taizong (Tang Taizong 唐太宗), who vigorously practiced benevolence and righteousness and personally brought about great peace; and Xianzong (Tang Xianzong 唐憲宗), who resented the accumulated abuses of generations, lamented the decline of the Tang house, excelled at employing loyal counsel, and was not led astray by the opinions of the crowd. At those times, the skill in planning and decisiveness of men like Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 and Du Ruhui 杜如晦, and the purity and uprightness of men like Li Jiang 李絳, all had much to recommend them. Coming to the Song's possession of the realm, rulers such as Taizu (Song Taizu 宋太祖), Taizong (Song Taizong 宋太宗), and Zhenzong (Song Zhenzong 宋真宗) all admired and yearned for high antiquity; and at those times there were the calm resolve of men like Zhao Pu 趙普, and the firm uprightness of men like Lü Mengzheng 呂蒙正 and Li Hang 李沆, who were likewise all sufficient to accomplish great things. With rulers and ministers meeting one another like this, the governance they achieved and the successes they accomplished ought to have been able to rival those of the Two Emperors and Three…

punctuated: 王也。然漢不免於雜伯，唐不免於雜夷，宋亦不過大綱正而萬目未盡舉。比之《詩》《書》所稱，所謂於變時雍，比屋可封，《關睢》《麟趾》之風，《鵲巢》《騶虞》之化，有所不及者，盖由其君徒欲其治而不求其道，徒有其志而不求其心；為之臣者，或於道有未聞，或用之未盡其才。此漢、唐、宋之治效所以止於漢、唐、宋而已也。洪惟天朝太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝丕隆大統於前，仁宗昭皇帝、宣宗章皇帝紹承令緒於後，咸以帝王之心而求帝王之道，以帝王之道而為帝王之治。所以舉斯世於雍煕泰和之域，措斯民於春臺玉燭之中。至治之盛，巍巍然而無加，蕩蕩乎其難名，誠有如陛下所言矣。陛下以聖繼聖，嗣大歷服，允懷繼述，夙夜匪遑，期與臣民咸躋煕皞。
translation_en:
… Kings. Yet the Han did not avoid admixing the ways of the hegemons, the Tang did not avoid admixing the customs of barbarians, and the Song merely rectified the main principles without fully attending to the myriad details. Compared with what is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of Documents (Shu)—what are called the universal transformation to timely harmony, households side by side all worthy of enfeoffment, the moral customs of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes, and the civilizing influence of the "Quechao" and "Zouyu" odes—the reason they fell short is that their rulers merely desired good governance without seeking its Way, and merely possessed the ambition without seeking its mind; as for those who served as their ministers, either they had not yet heard the Way, or when employed their talents were not fully exhausted. This is why the administrative achievements of the Han, Tang, and Song stopped at being merely those of the Han, Tang, and Song.

Reflecting reverently upon our August Dynasty: Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi) and Grand Ancestor the Cultured Emperor (Taizong Wen Huangdi) grandly exalted the great succession in the past, while Benevolent Ancestor the Brilliant Emperor (Renzong Zhao Huangdi) and Propagating Ancestor the Accomplished Emperor (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi) inherited and continued the fine patrimony thereafter. All of them, with the mind of the Emperors and Kings, sought the Way of the Emperors and Kings, and with the Way of the Emperors and Kings, carried out the governance of the Emperors and Kings. Thus they have raised this world into a realm of harmonious peace and supreme concord, and placed these people amidst the joyous prosperity of the "spring terrace" and the "jade candle." The flourishing of this consummate governance—so lofty that nothing can be added to it, so vast that it is difficult to name—is truly just as Your Majesty has stated.

Your Majesty, as a sage succeeding sages, has inherited the great succession and royal robes; sincerely cherishing the continuation and carrying forward of Your predecessors' work, from dawn to dusk You take no leisure, hoping together with Your ministers and people to ascend altogether into a state of bright and serene harmony.…

陛下之心即帝王兢兢業業求惟至道之心即
列聖敦崇古道以隆至治之心也
陛下以是心謹始而圖成推是心行之而得宜足以
為帝王之治又必拳拳以此策臣者夫豈徒哉
亦欲臣等而為帝王之臣也以臣之淺陋

之道陳之精一執中建中建極此帝王相傳授

陛下常存之於一心始終而不易則謹始圖成之要
豈不在茲歟脩身齊家治國平天下此帝王推
行之序也
陛下運之於一心循其序而行之則脩己安人之宜
夫豈不得乎此固

translation_en: Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind of the emperors and kings who cautiously and diligently sought only the supreme Way, and none other than the mind of the successive sacred ancestors who esteemed the ancient Way in order to exalt supreme governance. With this mind Your Majesty attends carefully to the beginning and plans for completion, and extends this mind to put it into practice appropriately, which suffices to achieve the governance of the emperors and kings. That You still earnestly put this policy question to Your servant—how could it be in vain? It is also because You wish Your servants to become ministers worthy of the emperors and kings. Shallow and crude as Your servant is, Your Majesty still looks upon him with the expectation of a minister of the emperors and kings; since Your Majesty possesses the virtue of a sage and occupies the position of a sage, how dare Your servant not set forth the Way of the emperors and kings? "Being refined and single-minded in holding fast to the Mean" and "establishing the Mean and establishing the supreme standard"—this is the method of the mind handed down from one to another by the emperors and kings. If Your Majesty constantly preserves it within Your single mind, unchanging from beginning to end, then does not the essential point of attending carefully to the beginning and planning for completion lie right here? "Cultivating the person, regulating the family, rightly governing the state, and making the whole empire tranquil and happy"—this is the sequence of implementation of the emperors and kings. If Your Majesty operates it within Your single mind and puts it into practice by following its sequence, then how could the appropriate measure for cultivating oneself and giving peace to others not be attained? This indeed is what Your august inquiry touched upon, and Your servant has prostrated himself and replied with a ten-thousandth part of it. At the end of this essay, Your servant presumes to offer something further. Your servant has earnestly observed that at the very beginning of Your Majesty's ascension to the throne, You opened the lectures of the Classics Colloquium, cut off the pleasures of idle amusements and excursions, constantly promulgated regulations for retrenchment and reduction, and repeatedly issued edicts of leniency and relief—this truly is keeping Your mind on the Way of the emperors and kings at the beginning. Your servant humbly prays that Your Majesty will maintain this mind from beginning to end, maintain this Way from beginning to end, and maintain this governance from beginning to end—establishing the great foundation and ordering the…

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
大經天地位而萬物育家稷契而俗鄒魯誠可
與二帝三王之治並美矣何成終之不可圖哉
若然非惟臣等幸甚實天下幸甚臣愚昧不足
以奉
大對惟
陛下少垂
睿覽臣不勝戰慄之至臣謹對

translation_en: … the great invariable relations, so that Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nourished, every family produces a Hou Ji or a Xie and the customs match those of Zou and Lu, then indeed Your rule can rival in beauty the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings—why then could bringing things to a successful completion not be achieved? If so, not only will your servants be most fortunate, but all under Heaven will truly be most fortunate! Your servant is ignorant and benighted, unworthy of presenting this grand response; I only pray that Your Majesty may deign to cast Your imperial gaze upon it. Overcome with fear and trembling to the utmost degree, your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
臣倪謙
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於道帝王之道具於經
經所以載道而心者又所以具是道之全體妙
是道之大用也故易以道陰陽即人心太極之
理也書以道政事即人心體用之跡也詩以理
性情即人心勸懲之道也春秋正名分即人心
褒貶之公也禮以節事樂以道志即人心中和
之理也唐虞三代之君所以繼天而立人極者
由其道具於心治本於道而底雍熙泰和之盛
漢唐以來之君所以莫能臻者由其心與道二
===
治與道違無怪其治之不古若也洪惟

punctuated:
臣倪謙。
臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，帝王之道具於經。經所以載道，而心者又所以具是道之全體，妙是道之大用也。故《易》以道陰陽，即人心太極之理也；《書》以道政事，即人心體用之跡也；《詩》以理性情，即人心勸懲之道也；《春秋》正名分，即人心褒貶之公也；《禮》以節事，《樂》以道志，即人心中和之理也。唐、虞、三代之君，所以繼天而立人極者，由其道具於心，治本於道，而底雍熙泰和之盛。漢、唐以來之君，所以莫能臻者，由其心與道二，治與道違，無怪其治之不古若也。洪惟太祖高皇帝膺天明命，撫有萬國，聖謨大訓，戒飭臣工，與古先哲王之道實相脗合。逮夫太宗文皇帝肅清內難，奠安宗社，萬幾之暇，表章六經，治道之盛，光前裕後。仁宗昭皇帝纘紹鴻業，宣宗章皇帝丕纘舊章，列聖相承，敦崇古道，以隆至治。巍乎成功，煥乎文章，
translation_en:
Your servant Ni Qian 倪謙.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is embodied in the Classics. The Classics are the vehicle that conveys the Way, while the mind is that which encompasses the whole substance of this Way and wondrously exercises its great function. Therefore, the Classic of Changes (Yi 易) speaks of yin and yang, which is none other than the principle of the Supreme Ultimate in the human mind; the Classic of Documents (Shu 書) speaks of affairs of governance, which are none other than the traces of substance and function in the human mind; the Classic of Odes (Shi 詩) regulates human nature and emotions, which is none other than the Way of encouragement and admonition in the human mind; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) rectifies names and statuses, which is none other than the impartiality of praise and blame in the human mind; the Record of Rites (Li 禮) moderates affairs and the Classic of Music (Yue 樂) expresses aspirations, which are none other than the principles of equilibrium and harmony in the human mind. The reason the rulers of Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and the Three Dynasties were able to succeed Heaven and establish the standard for humanity was that the Way was embodied in their minds and their governance was rooted in the Way, thereby attaining the flourishing of harmonious peace and supreme concord. The reason the rulers since the Han 漢 and Tang 唐 dynasties have been unable to reach this state is that their minds were separated from the Way and their governance departed from the Way; it is no wonder that their governance did not match that of antiquity.

Greatly reflecting upon how Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝), received the bright mandate of Heaven and pacified the myriad states, his sacred counsels and great instructions admonished the officials and were truly in complete accord with the Way of the ancient sage-kings. Coming down to Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong Wenhuangdi 太宗文皇帝), he cleared away internal troubles and brought stability to the ancestral altars; in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he honored and promoted the Six Classics, so that the flourishing of his Way of governance glorified his predecessors and enriched his successors. Emperor Zhao, the Benevolent Ancestor (Renzong Zhaohuangdi 仁宗昭皇帝), continued the great enterprise, and Emperor Zhang, the Propagating Ancestor (Xuanzong Zhanghuangdi 宣宗章皇帝), grandly carried on the established statutes. The successive sages inherited one from another, esteeming the ancient Way so as to exalt supreme governance. How lofty their achievements, how brilliant their cultural refinement, …

title: 正統四年進士登科錄
text:
猗歟盛哉伏惟
皇帝陛下嗣大歷服懋圖化理秉奉
天子民之誠隆繼志述事之孝道已躋於皇極世已
底於熈皞而猶不自滿假日引儒臣講論墳典
切劇治道廼復進臣等于
廷降賜
清問且以允懷繼述夙夜匪遑為言其與帝舜之
惟時惟幾成湯之日新又新文王日昃不暇成
王緝熈單心同一揆也臣雖愚昧敢不拜手稽
首以對揚
===
聖天子之明命臣聞六經未作而帝王之道具乎太
極六經既作而帝王之道載諸方策為治者固
不可離經以求道又豈能離道以出治哉孔子
生於周末有德無位懼三綱淪而九法斁也廼
退而刪詩書定禮樂賛周易脩春秋纂而成之
肇自唐虞訖于周以為萬世楷範書之精一執
中建中建極二帝三王之心法可舉而行也詩之
關睢麟趾王道之端周南之風化可舉而行也
易之分爻立象莫非治體之要春秋褒善貶惡
無非經國之典然六經之道同歸而禮樂之用

punctuated:
猗歟盛哉！伏惟皇帝陛下嗣大歷服，懋圖化理，秉奉天子民之誠，隆繼志述事之孝。道已躋於皇極，世已底於熈皞，而猶不自滿假，日引儒臣，講論墳典，切劇治道。廼復進臣等于廷，降賜清問，且以允懷繼述、夙夜匪遑為言，其與帝舜之惟時惟幾，成湯之日新又新，文王日昃不暇，成王緝熈單心，同一揆也。臣雖愚昧，敢不拜手稽首，以對揚聖天子之明命！

臣聞六經未作，而帝王之道具乎太極；六經既作，而帝王之道載諸方策。為治者，固不可離經以求道，又豈能離道以出治哉？孔子生於周末，有德無位，懼三綱淪而九法斁也，廼退而刪《詩》《書》，定《禮》《樂》，賛《周易》，脩《春秋》，纂而成之，肇自唐虞，訖于周，以為萬世楷範。《書》之精一執中、建中建極，二帝三王之心法，可舉而行也；《詩》之《關睢》《麟趾》，王道之端，周南之風化，可舉而行也；《易》之分爻立象，莫非治體之要；《春秋》褒善貶惡，無非經國之典。然六經之道同歸，而《禮》《樂》之用
translation_en:
…Oh, how glorious! I humbly reflect that Your Imperial Majesty, having succeeded to the great dynastic mandate and diligently planning for transformative governance, upholds the sincerity of serving Heaven and treating the people as Your children, and exalts the filial piety of carrying forward the intentions and continuing the enterprises of Your predecessors. Although the Way has already ascended to the August Ultimate and the world has already reached a state of prosperous tranquility, You still do not grow self-satisfied. Daily You summon Confucian officials to expound upon and discuss the ancient canons, earnestly deliberating on the Way of governance. Now You have furthermore advanced Your servant and others to the Court, bestowing upon us Your pure inquiry, and speaking of how You truly cherish carrying on the ancestral legacy, taking no leisure from morning to night. This is on the exact same principle as Emperor Shun's being attentive to the moment and to the subtle springs of action, Cheng Tang's daily renewal and ever-continuing renewal, King Wen's allowing himself no leisure even past midday, and King Cheng's continuing the bright virtue and applying his whole heart. Though Your servant is ignorant and benighted, how dare I not bow my head to the hands and knock my head to the ground to respond to and extol the bright mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven!

Your servant has heard that before the Six Classics were created, the Way of the Emperors and Kings was complete in the Supreme Ultimate; once the Six Classics were created, the Way of the Emperors and Kings was recorded on wooden tablets and bamboo slips. Those who govern certainly cannot depart from the Classics to seek the Way; how then could they depart from the Way to bring forth governance? Confucius was born at the end of the Zhou dynasty; possessing virtue but lacking office, and fearing that the Three Bonds would sink into oblivion and the Nine Categories of the Grand Norm would be ruined, he withdrew to edit the Odes (Shi) and the Documents (Shu), establish the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue), write commentaries on the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi), and compile the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). He compiled and completed them, beginning from Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun] and ending with the Zhou, to serve as a model for ten thousand generations. In the Documents, "being discerning and undivided, holding fast the Mean" and "establishing the Mean and establishing the Ultimate"—the method of the mind of the Two Emperors and Three Kings—can be taken up and put into practice. In the Odes, "Guanju" [sic, 關睢] and "Linzhi"—the beginning of the Kingly Way and the moral transformation of the Zhou South—can be taken up and put into practice. In the Changes, the division of lines and the establishment of images are none other than the essentials of the substance of governance; in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the praising of the good and censuring of the evil are nothing less than the standard canons for ordering the state. Yet while the Ways of the Six Classics converge on the same end, the application of Rites and Music…

text:
為急此孔子所以繼承往聖開萬世之太平也
爰暨漢唐以來賢智之君莫不景仰徽猷遹遵

為急。此孔子所以繼承往聖，開萬世之太平也。

爰暨漢唐以來，賢智之君莫不景仰徽猷，遹遵彝典，用圖治寧，咸有稱述。姑舉一二以實之：若漢武帝之罷黜百家、表章《六經》，光武之投戈講藝、息馬論道，唐太宗之《周禮》一書乙夜勤讀，固為美矣；其視堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武授受之心法，果何如哉？當時賢人君子出膺世用者，亦莫不獻忠效謀，以匡乃辟：若董仲舒以經術顯，汲黯以忠鯁著，鄧禹立功名於光武，魏徵勸仁義於太宗，固可尚矣；其視皋、夔、伊、傅、周、召都俞密勿之事業，果何如哉？是以考論漢唐君臣之治功，比之《詩》《書》所稱則有所不及者，以其雜伯雜夷，徒有願治之名，而無躬行之實以為致理之本也。

translation_en:
… is the most urgent. This is how Confucius carried on the legacy of the former sages and opened the way to great peace for ten thousand generations.

Coming down to the Han and Tang dynasties and thereafter, there were no worthy and wise rulers who did not look up in admiration to these fine counsels and follow the constant canons, thereby seeking governance and tranquility; all of them have things worthy of praise and recounting. Let me cite one or two examples to substantiate this: cases such as Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi 漢武帝) dismissing the Hundred Schools and exalting the Six Classics (Liujing), Emperor Guangwu (Guangwu 光武) casting aside his spear to lecture on the arts and resting his horse to discuss the Way, and Emperor Taizong of Tang (Tang Taizong 唐太宗) diligently reading the single book of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) into the second watch of the night—these were certainly admirable! Yet compared to the method of the mind-and-heart (xinfa) transmitted and received by Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, Tang 湯, King Wen 文, and King Wu 武, how do they really measure up? Among the worthy men and noble persons of those times who came forth to answer the needs of the age, there were likewise none who did not offer loyalty and contribute counsel to assist their sovereigns: cases such as Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 becoming illustrious through classical scholarship, Ji An 汲黯 becoming renowned for loyal outspokenness, Deng Yu 鄧禹 establishing merit and fame under Guangwu, and Wei Zheng 魏徵 urging benevolence and righteousness upon Taizong—these were certainly estimable! Yet compared to the achievements of Gao Yao 皋, Kui 夔, Yi Yin 伊, Fu Yue 傅, the Duke of Zhou 周, and the Duke of Shao 召 in harmonious deliberation and earnest diligence, how do they really measure up? Therefore, when we examine and discuss the governing achievements of the rulers and ministers of the Han and Tang, the reason they fall short compared to what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) is that they were adulterated with the ways of the霸 (hegemons) and of barbarians; they merely possessed the name of desiring good governance, without the reality of personal practice to serve as the foundation for bringing about order.

I reverently reflect that Your Majesty embodies the mind of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, honors the Way of the Six Classics and Confucius, and takes as a mirror the established statutes of the Imperial Ancestors in order to exalt the governance of great peace. Your mind and the Way mutually permeate one another; the Way and governance are at peace with one another. Rites, music, and moral transformation are nothing other than the manifestation of your spiritual energy and mental art; institutions, statutes, and cultural forms are none of them not the operation of your clear, numinous awareness. Therefore, that the Four Seas are well-ordered and tranquil, the myriad states are brought into harmony, and this age is raised to a state of prosperous serenity—all this is brought about by Your Majesty's tireless devotion from dawn to dusk and your personal practice. 成必有其要推行之序必有其宜臣鄙陋不足
以上揆
淵衷臣聞敬者聖學之所以成始而成終者也謹
始圖成之要其在於此乎中庸凡為天下國家

punctuated: 成，必有其要；推行之序，必有其宜。臣鄙陋，不足以上揆淵衷。臣聞敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也，謹始圖成之要，其在於此乎！《中庸》凡為天下國家有九經，而脩身為首，以及懷諸侯，推行之序，其在於斯乎！陛下修己以敬，其於謹始圖成而推行之者，皆已行之矣，尚何詢於微臣哉？然臣愚昧，既以敷陳於前矣，謹於終篇，竊有獻焉。伏願陛下始終此心，始終此敬，始終此治，追虞、周而比隆，陋漢、唐而不居，則聖治神功超越前古，斯民幸甚！天下幸甚！臣草茅微賤，荷蒙教育，其於致君澤民之方，固有志矣。伏望陛下俯垂采納，臣不勝戰慄屏營之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …completion must have its essential point, and the sequence of putting it into practice must have what is appropriate to it. Your servant is coarse and shallow, unequal to fathoming the depths of Your Majesty's mind. Yet your servant has heard that reverence is that whereby the learning of the sages completes both beginning and end—does the essential point of being careful at the beginning and planning for completion not lie in this? In the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), in all governance of the empire, the state, and the family there are nine standard rules, beginning with cultivating the person and extending to cherishing the feudal lords—does the sequence of putting it into practice not lie here? Your Majesty cultivates Yourself through reverence; as for being careful at the beginning, planning for completion, and putting these into practice, You have already carried them all out—what need is there still to inquire of this humble servant? Yet in my ignorance, having already set forth my views above, I respectfully presume at the close of this essay to offer a word: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will from beginning to end maintain this mind, from beginning to end maintain this reverence, and from beginning to end maintain this governance, emulating Yu [Shun] and the Zhou in equal splendor while disdaining the Han and Tang as unworthy of dwelling in. Then Your sacred governance and divine achievements will surpass all antiquity—how fortunate for the people, how fortunate for all under Heaven! Your servant, a lowly person from the rustic wilds, has been favored with Your nurturing education, and has long cherished the aspiration to find the means to serve his Sovereign and bring benefit to the people. I humbly hope that Your Majesty will condescend to accept these words. Your servant is overcome with trembling and anxious awe. Your servant respectfully replies.
